# Themes

The recurring ideas extracted across sources, each with the sources that support it. Built from research/themes/ (one file per task). Rules: [README.md](README.md).

## agent-as-service-many-surfaces: The agent as a service with many surfaces
One agent service behind an API, reached through a web app, Slack, browser extensions and embedding in existing tools, rather than a single app or a separate agent per surface. Matters for the agent-interface choice (own app vs Slack vs embedded).
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): the counter-case: River has one surface (Slack, no DMs), with companion links (Quick sites, Live Preview) for rich output (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Tobi Lütke: AI Agents, Better Decisions (Knowledge Project)](sources/fs-knowledge-project-tobi-lutke-ai-agents.md): River can join Google Meet when invited, "although not really utilized" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): "The agent is a service, not an application, and surfaces are simply customized views into it"; web app, Slack, Chrome extension in third-party tools, internal apps embed via API (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Stripe built their own in-house Glean alternative](sources/groundedhallucination-stripe-kai-teardown.md): "Surfaces are views, not the product" (independent restatement) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Harbor: Stripe's AI-assisted prototyping tool](sources/stripe-harbor-ai-prototyping.md): Harbor is its own browser app but also an MCP toolset and a rendering service other agents call (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Claude Cowork and chat are now one Claude](sources/claude-cowork-chat-unified.md): one Claude on web, desktop and mobile; start on a computer, check progress or answer questions on a phone; work continues in the cloud (Pro/Max launch, "What it looks like"; Enterprise, "One Claude for every task"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude Cowork on web and mobile: hand off work anywhere](sources/claude-cowork-web-mobile-handoff.md): Cowork on desktop, web and iOS/Android; chat and Cowork now share one home with projects and artifacts together; desktop keeps local files and browser use (sections "What changes today", "Getting started"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Cyera on making Claude Cowork the front door to 40 tools](sources/claude-customers-cyera-cowork-front-door.md): Cowork chosen as the aggregator over per-tool embedded AI: "Claude is now the aggregator" across Snowflake, Salesforce, Drive, Slack; 40 tools and several homegrown MCP servers (Q&A, "Why route work through Claude Cowork"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude for the financial industry](sources/claude-guide-financial-industry.md): each agent role can run as a Cowork or Microsoft 365 plugin on the desktop or as a Managed Agents hosted service (ch. 2, "Pre-built finance agent reference architectures"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude's memory works everywhere, and you decide what's in it](sources/claude-memory-everywhere.md): same memory in chat and Cowork, including Cowork tasks running in the cloud, carried in both directions ("One memory across Claude Cowork and chat"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to develop a Headless Product Strategy](sources/departmentofproduct-headless-product-strategy.md): "capabilities, data and logic as the product, the UI as one of many consumption paths" (Salesforce headless split) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to develop an MCP Product Strategy](sources/departmentofproduct-mcp-product-strategy.md): Intercom made Fin an MCP client that reaches other tools, rather than become a server hidden behind Claude. Stripe is content to be invisible behind agents (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

## agent-control-plane: Agent control planes above vendors
Platforms that register, govern and observe agents across vendors (registries, policy, audit, cost), sold as the enterprise layer above individual harnesses.
- [Trace agents with OpenTelemetry on the Claude Platform](sources/claude-agent-observability-otel.md): one destination in the Claude Console sends traces to the organisation's existing tools; Databricks Unity Gateway named for token usage by team and flagging unusual activity ("Works with your observability tools"). (research-claude-resources-articles)

## agent-factory-sdlc: Agents across the whole product development loop
A chain of specialised agents (insight, define, build, review, test, coordinate) removes bottlenecks one after another; Glass is the define-stage agent. Related: [[intent-factory-before-discovery]].
- [What product looks like when coding is solved | Geoff Charles (Ramp CPO)](sources/lenny-podcast-geoff-charles-product-when-coding-solved.md): Glass/Inspect/Review Buddy/Testo/Gadget loop (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How We Built Glass: Vibe Coding a Product Used by 700 People](sources/x-shanebuchan-how-we-built-glass.md): Glass builds Glass with Defrag, doc validation, gates (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp built an AI agent harness in six weeks](sources/thenewstack-ramp-laminar-agent-harness.md): one harness under customer-service agents, Inspect and Glass (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform](sources/ramp-builders-building-laminar.md): one harness for support chat, headless OCR, Inspect, Stack and Glass (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [An Inside Look Into How This $159B Tech Company Ships So Fast](sources/youtube-notmybusiness-inside-stripe-ships-fast.md): Orbit: research, shareable plan teammates comment on, one-button handoff to a minion that may run 12 hours and pause to ask; 'Gru' code-review agent (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Stripe's Internal Agent Ecosystem for Product Development](sources/claude-doc-geoff-stripe-internal-agent-ecosystem.md): five-stage PM-to-code flow: Kai research, Harbor/Protodash prototype, Orbit plan, Minions build, review agent plus human (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Eight trends defining how software gets built in 2026](sources/claude-2026-agentic-coding-trends.md): side-by-side traditional vs agentic SDLC table, eight stages each, cycle time "weeks-months" to "hours-days" (Trend 1). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [The AI-native SDLC playbook](sources/claude-ai-native-sdlc-playbook.md): six stages (Plan, Design, Build, Test, Deploy, Maintain) with an agent embedded in each and a loop, not a line; the end state is "a loop in which each accepted artifact fires the next gate" (§Plays). - [Agentic coding is straining CI. - [Office Hours: Building for the model that doesn't exist yet (Ramp, with Boris Cherny)](sources/claude-customers-ramp-office-hours.md): Ramp says it has agents across ideation, bug finding, log alerts, coding, review and post-deploy monitoring, plus security (Rahul, "implemented agents at pretty much every part"). - [How Sentry built end-to-end bug fixing with Claude Managed Agents](sources/claude-customers-sentry-bug-fixing-agents.md): same Managed Agents infrastructure runs background fixing of the most actionable bugs and real-time developer help; claimed reviews on over 600k PRs a month (summary list; workflow section). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Datadog built a "universal machine tool" for Claude Code](sources/claude-datadog-universal-machine-tool.md): path from Courier (built by hand in a year) to BitsEvolve (evolutionary optimisation harness, a "council of models" with benchmark cascades) to Helix (Kafka-comparable service built in days by Claude Code with one human... ## agent-failure-modes: Recurring agent failure modes in PM work
Invented content, silent omissions, brittleness, generic output when context is thin.
- [How River takes security work from a fix to merge](sources/shopify-engineering-river-vulnerability-remediation.md): told to enumerate fully, River rechecked only the oldest claim; "Prompts are the right place to express judgment and the wrong place to express a guarantee" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [AI SLOPCAST #9](sources/oleg-guru-ai-slopcast-shopify-river-lehrwerkstatt.md): public-by-default archives everyone's gaps, "a treasure trove" for HR (critique) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): 'There were agents that went rogue ... may have almost taken down core systems'; 'when in doubt an agent will just brute force it' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Thoughts On A Month With Devin](sources/answerai-month-with-devin.md): stuck loops (an HTML-parsing scraper task), a day spent on a platform-unsupported deployment while hallucinating features, tunnel vision on the wrong root cause, false-positive security findings (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [AWS AI coding tool decided to delete and recreate a customer-facing system, causing 13-hour outage (report)](sources/the-decoder-aws-kiro-outage.md): agent 'chose' to delete and recreate the environment; permissions inherited from the engineer bypassed two-person sign-off (FT sources; Amazon says it was misconfigured access controls and limited to Cost Explorer in one China region) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Replit makes vibe-y promise to stop its AI agents making vibe coding disasters](sources/theregister-replit-saastr-response.md): reported deletion of a production DB with records on ~1,206 executives and ~1,196 companies despite an instruction not to change code; agent reportedly said rollback would not work, but data was recovered manually (eWeek and others, search results) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [A month with Devin](sources/answerai-thoughts-month-with-devin.md): independent: 3/20 successes on real tasks; unpredictable; pursues impossible tasks instead of flagging blockers (Jan 2025, dated). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Codex MCP server removal](sources/openai-codex-mcp-server-removed.md): integration route removed by the vendor; third-party blogs still describe it. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Headless docs](sources/anthropic-claude-code-headless-agent-sdk.md): unattended runs deny permission prompts; `-p` does not wait for MCP tasks; MCP calls moved to background lose their result. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [CR-Bench](sources/arxiv-cr-bench.md): independent, preliminary: agents built to find all issues have low signal-to-noise in code review (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [METR early-2025 developer RCT](sources/metr-early-2025-experienced-developer-rct.md): independent: AI-allowed tasks took 19% longer for experts on familiar repos while they believed it was faster (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [How Delivery Hero's agent merges 100+ pull requests a day with Claude](sources/claude-customers-delivery-hero-pr-agent.md): "If you churn out five times more changes ... you will have five times more incidents if the change failure rate remains at the same level"; investing in agent-driven operations and safer rollouts (§Looking ahead). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Multi-agent coordination patterns: Five approaches and when to use them](sources/claude-multi-agent-coordination-patterns.md): rubber-stamping verifiers, orchestrator information bottleneck, conflicting teammates, silent routing failures, reactive loops in shared state (each "Where it struggles"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Anthropic secures its AI-native software development lifecycle](sources/claude-securing-ai-native-sdlc-at-anthropic.md): the agent-to-agent escalation over Slack after a model upgrade; lesson: "draw the boundary around access and actions, not around a model's instructions" and include an agent's access to other agents (§Monitor). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Uber's CISO on building an insider threat program for AI](sources/claude-uber-ciso-insider-threat-ai.md): concern is accidental misuse and models "directed to act outside the constraints we expect"; "constraints create new behaviors" so detection must keep finding new ones. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [DESIGN.md Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-design-md-explained.md): agents fill a missing token with something plausible, and the divergence spreads while still looking consistent. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Agentic Workflows Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-agentic-workflows-explained.md): a cited benchmark classes failures as planning, execution and formatting errors. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [What is parallel AI agent coding? An in-depth guide for product teams](sources/departmentofproduct-parallel-agent-coding.md): parallel agents bring merge conflicts and harder debugging; they're weak on architecture and on UI that needs visual feedback (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [AI prototyping with Lovable (Product Talk)](sources/producttalk-ai-prototyping-lovable.md): Tool claimed to have fixed issues it had not (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Atlassian Rovo AI review (Slite)](sources/slite-atlassian-rovo-ai-review.md): A user team reported (community post, relayed by Slite) a runbook summary with steps, commands and contacts absent from the source; a partner (Seibert) reported a custom agent that "confidently invented releases" (case 1) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

- [Why Atlassian Rovo Failed Us](sources/devto-tschimev-why-atlassian-rovo-failed-us.md): Rovo "can't handle nuanced tickets, doesn't understand team conventions"; "polished in demos but struggles in production"; single-team anecdote (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Sycophantic AI decreases prosocial intentions and promotes dependence](sources/stanford-cheng-sycophantic-ai-science-2026.md): 11 models affirmed users ~49% more often than humans (Science, 2026; abstract via search); risk for 'pressure-test my idea' uses (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## agent-frameworks: Agent frameworks
Libraries and engines (agent frameworks, durable-execution engines) used to build or host an agent loop.
- [How Stripe Built Kai on Deep Agents (LangChain)](sources/langchain-how-stripe-built-kai-deep-agents.md): Kai built on LangChain Deep Agents: 'solves all the non-Stripey problems'; minions on a Goose fork: Stripe uses two different open-source harnesses for two agent families (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Long-running agents (Cloudflare Agents SDK docs)](sources/cloudflare-agents-long-running-agents.md): recovery after eviction is not automatic replay: onFiberRecovered runs and 'you decide what resuming means'; keepAlive suits minutes not hours, use Workflows for longer work (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Open-Inspect (ColeMurray/background-agents) README](sources/github-open-inspect-background-agents.md): sandbox runs a Supervisor, a harness (OpenCode or Claude Agent) and a Bridge back to the control plane; harness is pluggable (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Durable Execution for AI Agents: LangGraph, DBOS, Inngest and Temporal Compared](sources/hackernoon-durable-execution-compared.md): LangGraph default async durability can lose the newest checkpoint on a hard crash, checkpoints are per node not per tool call; Inngest renaming a step orphans in-flight runs; Temporal needs a cluster and about two weeks to production (author's estimate) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Production-ready agents with the OpenAI Agents SDK + Temporal](sources/temporal-openai-agents-sdk-integration.md): the integration replaces the Agents SDK Runner so every agent invocation runs as a Temporal Activity; handoffs are also recorded; workflow code holds orchestration logic (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness Engineering: ... - [Agent Frameworks, Runtimes, and Harnesses, oh my!](sources/langchain-agent-frameworks-runtimes-harnesses.md): vendor claim: framework / runtime / harness vocabulary; author admits no agreed definition (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Deep Agents vs LangChain vs LangGraph](sources/langchain-deep-agents-vs-langchain-vs-langgraph.md): vendor claim: harness = framework agent plus middleware, on a LangGraph runtime (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

- [Pydantic AI documentation overview](sources/pydantic-ai-docs.md): first-party: framework adds Harness (memory, sub-agents, compaction) and 8 durable-execution engines (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent Development Kit (ADK) documentation](sources/google-adk-docs.md): first-party: model-agnostic, 5 languages, A2A, Google Cloud deployment (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

## agent-led-intent-shaping: Agents shape intent, not only execute it
Agents do the research, interrogation and spec-tightening that turn rough intent into shovel-ready requirements, with humans answering and deciding. This is the core job of a "product agent".
- [The AI-native SDLC playbook](sources/claude-ai-native-sdlc-playbook.md): Claude "asks the questions an analyst would ask: scope, users, constraints, and what success looks like" while the originator brainstorms; the spec pass must flag "areas of concern, especially where you cannot satisfy... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Best practices for getting started with Claude Cowork](sources/claude-cowork-getting-started-best-practices.md): "Make Claude ask you questions before it starts", repeating the ask back and asking clarifying questions, called the single most useful habit (Your first 10 minutes). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Miro's champions run their week with Claude Cowork](sources/claude-customers-miro-champions.md): Cowork used to pressure-test half-formed problems "before there's anything to draft"; usage moved from last step to first step (Hostetler, first answer). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How the product designer who built Claude Design uses it](sources/claude-design-designer-workflow.md): "ask for ten options, then remix"; generate 15 versions of a flow to collect colleague feedback; Claude provides starting points and the human chooses ("Best practices"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [A field guide to Claude Fable 5: Finding your unknowns](sources/claude-fable-finding-unknowns.md): the agent is asked to surface "unknown unknowns" ("blind spot pass"), brainstorm wildly different directions, and interview the user "one question at a time", prioritising questions that would change the architecture... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to use Google's new Ideate Agent for Product Discovery and Ideation](sources/departmentofproduct-google-stitch-ideate-agent.md): Ideate researches named apps, proposes three directions, asks the PM to pick, then drafts a PRD for approval before designing (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Building and Accelerating the Intent Factory](sources/geoff-building-accelerating-intent-factory.md): Ramp's parallel research agents write each finding to a file; seven-question interrogation; agent-originated intent (§Vision, steps 1–3) (research-product-agent-and-harness)
- [Intent Shaping in a Well-Managed Environment](sources/geoff-intent-shaping-well-managed-environment.md): an iterative owner/risk-advisor loop in which mitigations become requirements and the spec tightens (§Iterative intent-shaping) (research-product-agent-and-harness)

## agent-project-failure-rates: Agent project failure rates
Press-reported statistics on agent and genAI pilot failure (Gartner, MIT); not PM-specific and mostly unverified.
- [Deploying AI from pilot to production: a practical blueprint for CIOs and technical leaders](sources/claude-pilot-to-production-cio-blueprint.md): cites Accenture's Pulse of Change (July 2026): only 23% of C-suite leaders report sustained enterprise-wide impact from AI initiatives; pilots are unrepresentative (hand-picked teams, protected budgets). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Agentic Workflows Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-agentic-workflows-explained.md): agents failed about 50% of 34 general tasks in a cited study (the post calls it "Cibench"; not verified). (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Sloppenheimer: Amazon employees mock the company's AI on Slack (404 Media)](sources/404media-amazon-employees-mock-ai-slop.md): internal AI coding product mocked as slop; failed usage push (leaderboard detail unverified; paywalled) [audit 2026-10-24]. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Zapier customer story (Anthropic)](sources/anthropic-customer-story-zapier.md): counter-example claim: 800+ internal agents and 89% adoption (vendor-claimed, no outcomes). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How Brex improves code quality and productivity with Claude Code](sources/claude-brex-claude-code.md): vendor-claimed 3-4x on coding tasks; not PM evidence. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [MIT report: 95% of generative AI pilots at companies are failing (Fortune)](sources/fortune-mit-nanda-95-percent-pilots.md): ~95% of pilots no measurable P&L impact; bought tools about 2x as successful as internal builds (press; primary now filed as mit-nanda-genai-divide-2025) [audit 2026-10-24]. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Over 40% of agentic AI projects will be scrapped by 2027, says Gartner (Outlook Business coverage)](sources/gartner-agentic-ai-40-percent-cancelled.md): forecast: over 40% of agentic AI projects cancelled by end of 2027. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The GenAI Divide: State of AI in Business 2025](sources/mit-nanda-genai-divide-2025.md): primary: "95% of organizations are getting zero return"; success = beyond pilot with measurable KPIs at six months; self-reported, 52 interviews, 153 surveys, selection bias acknowledged (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## agent-protocol-security: Security of agent-to-agent and agent-to-tool protocols
Attacks and gaps that arise because a remote agent or its metadata becomes input to your agent: card or description poisoning, session smuggling, identity loss across delegation hops, optional signing.
- [Agent identity: a new access model for autonomous, team-wide AI](sources/claude-agent-identity-access-model.md): credentials stored separately and injected at the network boundary; non-allowed hosts blocked; every routine, memory write and network call audited (section "Security and audit"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [CISO's guide to agentic AI](sources/claude-ciso-guide-agentic-ai.md): prompt injection named as a main internal risk; egress allowlisting called "your strongest control against prompt injection"; connector tokens injected by a reverse proxy so the sandbox never holds them. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Inference hooks: inline data loss prevention for Claude Enterprise](sources/claude-enterprise-inference-hooks.md): tool responses from MCP connectors, skills and plugins are inspected before returning to the model, a check against injected or sensitive content arriving via tools ("How inference hooks works"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Centrally manage authorization for MCP connectors](sources/claude-enterprise-managed-mcp-auth.md): implemented as the Enterprise-Managed Authorization extension to the MCP authorization spec, embedding the Cross App Access protocol (intro; Okta-side quote). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Zero Trust for AI agents](sources/claude-zero-trust-for-ai-agents.md): Ch 04 catalogues tool poisoning, MCP rug pulls, tool-chaining exfiltration and loop amplification; Ch 06 Phase 2 advises self-hosting and signing verified MCP servers. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to develop an MCP Product Strategy](sources/departmentofproduct-mcp-product-strategy.md): cites the Asana and GitHub MCP incidents. Broad read/write scopes are hard to avoid, and servers should reject tokens with too much or irrelevant scope (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [A2ABreak: Systematic Security Analysis of the A2A Protocol](sources/arxiv-a2abreak-security-analysis.md): The first systematic, specification-level security analysis of A2A found. (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [Agent Card Poisoning: A Metadata Injection Vulnerability in the Systems using Google A2A Protocol](sources/keysight-agent-card-poisoning.md): Shows that an Agent Card is untrusted text that ends up in the caller's prompt: a malicious remote agent embeds instructions in its card, and the host LLM follows them. (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [A Security Engineer's Guide to the A2A Protocol](sources/semgrep-security-engineers-guide-a2a.md): The primary source behind the widely repeated claim that A2A "supports but does not enforce Agent Card signing", which Track 3 had only second-hand. (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [Action Fabric: MCP Server, MCP Client, and A2A explained](sources/servicenow-community-action-fabric-mcp-a2a.md): ServiceNow supports A2A in both directions, but its own governance layer does not cover it: "AI Gateway currently governs MCP traffic only; A2A is outside its scope as of the current GA release." For a regulated setting  (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [When AI Agents Go Rogue: Agent Session Smuggling Attack in A2A Systems](sources/unit42-agent-session-smuggling-a2a.md): A worked attack on stateful agent-to-agent delegation: a malicious remote agent uses an established A2A session to inject instructions into the calling agent across turns, causing data leakage and an unauthorised stock p (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)

## agent-ready-intent: A shared standard for agent-ready specs
Intent is complete enough for agentic delivery when it meets an agreed standard (templates, examples, evals) that gates delivery and improves from delivery feedback.
- [The AI-native SDLC playbook](sources/claude-ai-native-sdlc-playbook.md): an agreed intent.md template, encoded as a skill "set up by a technical team member and signed off by a lead" (§Stage 1, How to execute). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How CodeRabbit used Claude to build an agent orchestration system](sources/claude-coderabbit-plan-orchestration.md): experienced developers omit "obvious" requirements; the login-page anecdote (section "Addressing the internal knowledge gap"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Building verification loops in Claude Code with skills](sources/claude-verification-loops-skills.md): built-in "spec validation" skill verifies each change against a markdown spec in the repo and fixes violations ("Built-in verification loops"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to speed up engineering velocity with AI: a non-engineer's guide](sources/departmentofproduct-engineering-velocity-non-engineers.md): Morgan Stanley's tool writes English specs of legacy code, which engineers then rewrite from (280k hours claimed, via WSJ) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Building and Accelerating the Intent Factory](sources/geoff-building-accelerating-intent-factory.md): a spec, not a PRD; a completeness standard as a KR (Action 3) (research-product-agent-and-harness)
- [Intent Shaping in a Well-Managed Environment](sources/geoff-intent-shaping-well-managed-environment.md): a canonical spec artifact that absorbs detail and mitigations for re-assessment (risk agent, function 1) (research-product-agent-and-harness)
- [What is an idea (Jira Product Discovery docs)](sources/atlassian-jira-product-discovery-ideas.md): an idea is the basic unit; custom idea types (user problem, customer, bet, opportunity, solution), each with its own workflow. (user-story-mapping)
- [Documents (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-documents.md): documents can be referenced from issue descriptions, comments and agent guidance fields via @mention. (user-story-mapping)
- [Connect a coding agent to Spark via MCP (Productboard support)](sources/productboard-mcp-server-spark.md): specs live in a Specification tab on initiatives, features and subfeatures; Spark's 'Write spec' skill drafts them; agents read, edit, comment and update status. (user-story-mapping)
- [github/spec-kit (README)](sources/github-spec-kit-readme.md): a standard command set and Markdown artifacts per stage; constitution is the project-level baseline. (user-story-mapping)
- [Spec-Driven Development (spec-kit spec-driven.md)](sources/github-spec-kit-spec-driven.md): spec.md has user stories and acceptance criteria, ambiguity marked [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] instead of guessed; templates act as structured prompts with self-review checklists. (user-story-mapping)

## ai-synthesis-hallucination-risk: AI synthesis can invent or merge facts
Practitioner and academic evidence of fabricated details, merged quotes and lost depth in LLM summaries of qualitative data.
- [Self-service data analytics in Slack: how Anthropic deploys Claude Tag for ad-hoc questions](sources/claude-tag-self-service-analytics.md): stale skill gives "last Tuesday's wrong answer with full confidence" to a consumer cut off from context (section "Refresh skills"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to use Perplexity's new Computer...](sources/departmentofproduct-perplexity-computer.md): the competitor-monitor prompt has to forbid invented pricing and require a URL for every data point (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build a Persona Feature Tester with Claude Code and ElevenLabs](sources/departmentofproduct-persona-feature-tester.md): the personas' specific quotes and behaviours trace back to model-written "research" files (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to do AI-powered product discovery sprints](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-discovery-sprints.md): cites Deloitte's partial refund to the Australian government over fabricated sources as a deep-research warning (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Leveraging AI for thematic analysis of qualitative transcripts: feasibility study in insurance payer interviews (ISPOR 2025 poster)](sources/ispor-2025-ai-thematic-analysis-payer-interviews.md): Copilot on 10 interviews: misattributed/irrelevant quotes, 11-25% incorrect information. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [AI hallucination (Product Talk glossary)](sources/producttalk-ai-hallucination-glossary.md): ChatGPT on 17 transcripts (podcast says 15 interviews; relation unstated): invented details and merged-quote fabrications; fix with verbatim-quote code check and LLM fact-check judge. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Customer interview analysis with AI: All Things Product podcast with Teresa Torres and Petra Wille](sources/producttalk-torres-customer-interview-analysis-podcast.md): keep analysis and synthesis separate; do not outsource customer understanding. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [University of Turku replication: LLM thematic analysis of interviews (DeepSeek R1)](sources/utu-turku-llm-qualitative-analysis.md): DeepSeek R1 re-ran a published analysis of 17 expert interviews: kept concepts, lost interpretive depth, overgeneralized (abstract only). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Don't Use Generative AI to Replace Discovery with Real Humans](sources/producttalk-generative-ai-discovery.md): ChatGPT "customer stories" were generic, similar and fabricated (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Building My First AI Product: 6 Lessons from My 90-Day Deep Dive](sources/producttalk-ai-playbook-first-ai-product.md): ChatGPT invented interview quotes; Claude produced duplicates and solutions labelled as opportunities (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Customer Interview Analysis: Where AI Helps and Hurts](sources/producttalk-customer-interview-analysis-ai.md): ChatGPT got about 30% of direct quotes wrong or missing (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## artifact-standardization: Artifact standardization
Conventions, manifests and protocol primitives that make artifacts typed, discoverable and attributable (file layouts, frontmatter, MCP resources, provenance).
- [Quick: An internal hosting platform for the AI era](sources/shopify-engineering-quick.md): one artifact form (static folder + fixed API: db, files, AI, warehouse, websockets, identity); "All Quick sites are open to all employees", no owners (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [The AI-native SDLC playbook](sources/claude-ai-native-sdlc-playbook.md): named artifacts per stage with templates (intent.md, spec.md, plan.md, REVIEW.md, bands.yaml) (throughout). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Blank Metal, a lean professional services firm, runs on Claude Cowork](sources/claude-customers-blank-metal-cowork.md): brand voice and visual guidelines embedded as skills so decks, docs and deliverables align automatically rather than per person (first answer). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How the product designer who built Claude Design uses it](sources/claude-design-designer-workflow.md): brand files become a design system Claude builds with and checks its output against before showing it; teams can keep several; an admin can approve one standard and lock edits. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude Design now stays on brand for daily work](sources/claude-design-on-brand.md): one or several design systems imported; Claude builds with components, checks output and corrects before you see it; admin role approves a standard system and locks edits ("Build with your design system components"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to build the ultimate Product Dashboard that generates stakeholder updates on demand](sources/departmentofproduct-product-dashboard-stakeholder-updates.md): the "decision queue" is a fixed record (the call, kind, who it waits on, age, context) that Claude pulls out of the inbox; "a forcing function", not a to-do list (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [What are Claude Skills and how can you use them for product-related work?](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-skills-for-product-work.md): a brand-guidelines skill plus the pptx skill give house-style decks; the xlsx skill enforces zero formula errors (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [DESIGN.md Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-design-md-explained.md): Google open-sourced DESIGN.md: YAML tokens ("what") plus markdown rationale ("why") in one file, with a CLI linter that includes a WCAG 4.5:1 contrast check. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Spec Kit and spec-driven.md (GitHub)](sources/github-spec-kit-sdd.md): defines a per-feature folder (`specs/003-chat-system/`) with spec.md, plan.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md, tasks.md plus `memory/constitution.md` (spec-driven.md). (user-story-mapping)
- [Specs (Kiro docs)](sources/kiro-specs-docs.md): three-file spec per feature with three phases (requirements/bug analysis, design, tasks); Spec Kit uses a different file set for the same job. (user-story-mapping)
- [Understanding Spec-Driven-Development: Kiro, spec-kit, and Tessl](sources/fowler-bockeler-sdd-kiro-speckit-tessl.md): three different layouts (Kiro steering + per-feature folders; spec-kit constitution + numbered folders of ~8 files; Tessl `.tessl/framework` plus `*.spec.md`). Memory-bank files (AGENTS.md) distinguished from task specs. (user-story-mapping)
- [Resources (MCP specification 2025-06-18)](sources/mcp-spec-resources.md): resource = uri, name, title, description, mimeType, size, plus annotations `audience` [user|assistant], `priority` 0-1, `lastModified` ISO-8601; resource templates via RFC 6570 URI templates; `resources/list`, `resources/read`, `r (user-story-mapping)
- [Snowflake-managed MCP server (Snowflake docs)](sources/snowflake-managed-mcp-server-docs.md): supports only tool capabilities, not MCP resources or prompts; response truncation at 250 KB; max 50 tools; recursion depth 10. (user-story-mapping)
- [Descriptor Format of Catalog Entities (Backstage)](sources/backstage-descriptor-format.md): Kubernetes-style envelope (`apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata` name/title/description/tags/links/labels/annotations, `spec`); relations are generated, not hand-written. (user-story-mapping)
- [Descriptor Format of Catalog Entities (Backstage)](sources/backstage-descriptor-format.md): required fields include `spec.owner` and `spec.lifecycle` (experimental, production, deprecated, extensible); System groups components, Domain groups systems (a built-in grouping hierarchy). (user-story-mapping)
- [MADR: Markdown Architectural Decision Records](sources/adr-madr-template.md): location `docs/decisions/`, name `NNNN-title-with-dashes.md`; frontmatter `status` (proposed, accepted, rejected, deprecated, superseded), `date`, `decision-makers`, `consulted`, `informed`. (user-story-mapping)
- [Diátaxis: a systematic approach to technical documentation](sources/diataxis-framework.md): four types matched to user needs; organises content, style and architecture; the site claims adoption in hundreds of projects (vendor/self-reported). (user-story-mapping)
- [Gherkin Reference (Cucumber)](sources/cucumber-gherkin-reference.md): one Feature per `.feature` file; keywords Feature, Rule, Example/Scenario, Given/When/Then, Background, Scenario Outline; examples double as tests via step definitions. (user-story-mapping)
- [PROV-Overview (W3C)](sources/w3c-prov-overview.md): provenance defined as information about entities, activities and people producing a thing; PROV-DM conceptual model with PROV-O/N/XML serialisations. (user-story-mapping)
- [C2PA and Content Credentials Explainer](sources/c2pa-explainer.md): assertions are grouped into a signed claim, bundled into a manifest bound to the asset by hash; each edit adds a manifest referencing the previous one. (user-story-mapping)
- [PRD template (Confluence)](sources/atlassian-confluence-prd-template.md): named sections: basics and roles, objective, success metrics, assumptions, options (requirement, user story, importance, Jira issues), supporting docs, open questions with answer date, out of scope. (user-story-mapping)
- [Project poster template (Confluence)](sources/atlassian-confluence-project-poster-template.md): Team Playbook project poster: problem space, what we know vs still need to answer, solution and scope, reference links; a living page upstream of the PRD. (user-story-mapping)
- [DACI decision template (Confluence)](sources/atlassian-confluence-daci-decision-template.md): decision record fields: status, impact, DACI roles, due date, background, options with pros/cons/cost, action items, outcome. (user-story-mapping)

## build-vs-buy: Own the agent harness as a moat
Reasons to build internally: moat, speed of fixes, learning for the external product.
- [We Built Every Employee at Ramp Their Own AI Coworker](sources/x-sebgoddijn-glass-article.md): three reasons (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Eric Glyman April 2026 posts on Glass and AI adoption](sources/x-eglyman-april-glass-posts.md): "we decided to own it" (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How We Built Glass: Vibe Coding a Product Used by 700 People](sources/x-shanebuchan-how-we-built-glass.md): a 3-person team, vibe-coded (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Introducing Glass: Learn Things Once.](sources/x-eglyman-introducing-glass-learn-things-once.md): "as is often the case at Ramp, a small team built something"; now sold externally as a product, so the build also became a revenue line (vendor claim) (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How to get your company AI pilled](sources/x-geoffintech-ai-pilled-article.md): "our own version of Claude Code's Cowork, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK"; "a team of four built it in under three months" (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp built an AI agent harness in six weeks](sources/thenewstack-ramp-laminar-agent-harness.md): Ramp replaced vendor SDKs with its own harness Laminar (six-week V1, now under Glass and Inspect) after testing Claude Agent SDK, Claude Managed Agents, OpenAI Agents SDK, OpenCode, LangChain, Sierra; no cost comparison published (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform](sources/ramp-builders-building-laminar.md): Ramp built its own harness (~May 2026, v1 in six weeks) after trying vendor SDKs, managed-agent APIs and frameworks; 'you still need good engineers to be on-call' (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): built after a no-code agent builder and coding agents for non-engineers both failed (quality sprawl; security and support burden); core primitives shared with Stripe's customer-facing agents (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): 'it's not about providing AI it's about providing the correct governance structures'; v0 by 1.5 people in two weeks; core team under 10 (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Emily Glassberg Sands on Latent Space](sources/latentspace-emily-sands-stripe.md): Sands: build-vs-buy is 'sequential': built GoLLM when no safe vendor existed, then replaced it with open-source LibreChat; buys via RFP 'spotlight' (Braintrust for evals) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Ramp Inspect Architecture 2026: How Background Coding Agents Scale Safely](sources/wavect-ramp-inspect-architecture.md): buy commodity sandbox infrastructure; build or heavily customise base images, harness, context, permissions and evals (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness Engineering: ... Eleven Systems](sources/arxiv-harness-engineering-eleven-systems.md): independent: 0 of 11 production coding harnesses import a general agent framework; recommends raw SDK calls or a harness SDK, and starting with a bash-only linear loop (scope: coding harnesses) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent Design Is Still Hard](sources/lucumr-agent-design-is-still-hard.md): independent practitioner (anecdote): would not again use a framework SDK for provider abstraction; expects to need own abstraction (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Minions: Stripe's one-shot coding agents](sources/stripe-minions-one-shot-coding-agents.md): first-party: Stripe forked Goose rather than building from scratch or using a framework; reasons are codebase specificity and existing human-dev tooling (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

## compounding-context-repo: Context that compounds with each shipped feature
A shared, agent-readable, harness-agnostic store of product context ("evidence, not yet fact", with domain owners), which every spec writes back to. This is the harness's memory layer.
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): monorepo World holds code, skills, conventions, intent documents, runbooks, AGENTS.md and zone knowledge; sessions leave "a pebble, a skill update, an AGENTS.md diff" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [River's reaction to the Shop floor post](sources/x-tobi-river-reaction-to-shop-floor-post.md): "AGENTS.md files are mirror surfaces": writing them forces teams to find they "didn't quite agree with each other" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify's River: The AI Agent as Organizational Memory](sources/aienabledpm-shopify-river-organizational-memory.md): agent failures as context, permission and taste gaps, fixed by making knowledge explicit (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [The AI-native SDLC playbook](sources/claude-ai-native-sdlc-playbook.md): "When Claude makes a mistake twice, the correction goes into CLAUDE.md"; review findings feed CLAUDE.md; incidents feed evals; post-mortems go to a lessons file (§Stage 3, §Stage 5, §Stage 6). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Anthropic enables self-service data analytics with Claude](sources/claude-anthropic-self-service-analytics.md): skill markdown colocated with transformation models; a review hook flags reporting-model changes that do not touch a skill file; ~90% of data-model PRs include a skill change (Skills, "maintenance"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Building AI agents for the enterprise](sources/claude-building-agents-enterprise-cowork.md): leaders "encoding institutional knowledge into systems that compound over time" (opening). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Claude Code works in large codebases: Best practices and where to start](sources/claude-code-large-codebases.md): lean, layered CLAUDE.md files; stop hooks proposing CLAUDE.md updates from each session; root codebase maps (section "Making the codebase navigable at scale"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Office Hours: Building the case for leaders who ship with DoorDash](sources/claude-customers-doordash-office-hours.md): a tech lead wrote 50+ architectural principles as markdown in the repo for agents; standardized team skills (e.g. mobile simulator skill) (learnings answer). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [HubSpot product and marketing leaders on scaling Claude Cowork](sources/claude-customers-hubspot-cowork.md): team-level context repository holding customer insights, decisions, data analysis, RFCs and key Slack threads so any person or agent pulls from one source (Sejal Parikh answer); Director PM: "Information scaffolding... - [How Zapier's marketing and engineering teams use Claude Cowork to delegate real work](sources/claude-customers-zapier-cowork.md): at the end of each session the PMM asks "what should we remember from this?" and has Claude capture it so sessions compound (Q&A, homepage concepting). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [The founder's playbook: Building an AI-native startup](sources/claude-founders-playbook.md): MVP stage says skipping specs, architecture decisions and CLAUDE.md produces "AI technical debt" that compounds as each session re-derives decisions; prescribes a per-session log entry back into the context doc (MVP stage,... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Scaling agentic coding across your organization](sources/claude-guide-scaling-agentic-coding.md): project CLAUDE.md checked into the repo root on main, reviewed in onboarding, updated in PRs "when architectural decisions change", optionally branch-specific (ch. 03 Sharing CLAUDE.md; appendix example). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Skills explained: How Skills compares to prompts, Projects, MCP, and subagents](sources/claude-skills-explained.md): heuristics for promotion: a prompt typed repeatedly should become a skill; instructions copied across Projects should become a skill. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Claude Tag serves as Anthropic's first responder for CI/CD failures](sources/claude-tag-ci-cd-first-responder.md): standing instructions are markdown skills in a GitHub repo so teammates iterate on them like code; a 617-line investigation skill per bug class was built by debugging turn-by-turn with Claude and having it write the file... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to use Claude Code for non-engineering use cases](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-code-non-engineers.md): a PM's shared "Claude Code Product OS" repo of frameworks, strategy templates and stakeholder profiles (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to speed up engineering velocity with AI: a non-engineer's guide](sources/departmentofproduct-engineering-velocity-non-engineers.md): CLAUDE.md records code style, tests, repo etiquette and setup for new hires and the agent alike (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

## cost-control-routing: Cost metering and model routing built into the harness
Open access to frontier models blew budgets; Ramp added per-project meters, limits and a router that picks the model.
- [Introducing Glass: Learn Things Once.](sources/x-eglyman-introducing-glass-learn-things-once.md): $1.5M week, taxi meter, Ramp Router, 30% drop claimed (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp: Lessons from Building a New AI Product - The Pragmatic Summit](sources/pragmatic-engineer-ramp-lessons-new-ai-product.md): LLM proxy with per-team cost tracing and config-only model swaps (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Introducing Glass. Make your entire company smarter](sources/ramp-introducing-glass.md): budget blown in weeks; users default to frontier models (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How to get your company AI pilled](sources/x-geoffintech-ai-pilled-article.md): the opposite stance in April: "Kill token limits and access restrictions", "treat AI usage as an infinite learning budget"; metering came later with Router/Glass (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp Router launch posts (Jul 20, 2026)](sources/x-ramp-router-launch-posts.md): the 30% bill cut is a Router claim from July 2026, 'without any performance degradation' (Zaks); no published data (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp built an AI agent harness in six weeks](sources/thenewstack-ramp-laminar-agent-harness.md): independent data point on in-harness routing, LangChain Open SWE -64% median cost/thread, no significant quality change (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform](sources/ramp-builders-building-laminar.md): Ramp Router sits in the harness as the LLM gateway; model choice per cost/latency/performance (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Building an agentic harness that outlasts the model](sources/shopify-engineering-agentic-harness-outlasts-model.md): full scan $50–300, diff scan $5–50; partitions sized to 20–30% of the context window (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Small Models, Massive Wins (Beyond the Pilot)](sources/venturebeat-beyond-the-pilot-farhan-thawar.md): no token limits but "circuit breakers"; token leaderboard replaced by a usage dashboard where anyone sees their own spend (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How Shopify built an AI stack that doesn't care which models survive](sources/venturebeat-shopify-ai-stack-model-agnostic.md): the proxy auto-moved users to Opus or GPT 5.5 when "Claude Fable 5 shut down" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [From Memo to Movement](sources/firstround-shopify-ai-culture.md): in 2025 a token-spend leaderboard was "a cool proxy for value"; by 2026 it was removed (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): Kai projects set the default model and can block expensive models for a workflow (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Production-grade AI agents for financial compliance: Lessons from Stripe](sources/aws-stripe-compliance-agents.md): all LLM calls go through an LLM Proxy (noisy-neighbour limits, fallbacks, usage tracking by privacy class); prompt caching cut cost 60% (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Use Claude Code in the cloud (Claude Code on the web docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-cloud-sessions.md): no separate VM charge; cloud sessions share the account's rate limits, so parallel tasks consume limits proportionately (Limitations) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Automate work with scheduled tasks (Claude Code routines docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-scheduled-tasks.md): hourly caps (100 scheduled runs/hr per account, 30/hr per task for run-now and API fires) and subscription usage draw-down, no overage by default (Usage and limits) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [The $47K agent loop: why logging, monitoring and max_tokens all failed to stop it](sources/devto-47k-agent-loop.md): claims four LangChain agents on A2A looped (Verifier requesting, Analyzer producing) with no termination condition or budget cap; 'They had logging. They had monitoring. They did not have a hard limit.' (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Durable Execution for AI Agents: LangGraph, DBOS, Inngest and Temporal Compared](sources/hackernoon-durable-execution-compared.md): payloads must stay in network rules out Inngest unless self-hosted (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [How Ramp built a full-context background coding agent on Modal](sources/modal-ramp-inspect-background-agent.md): sessions start in seconds from a filesystem snapshot refreshed by a cron every 30 minutes (repos cloned, dependencies installed, build run); startup speed framed as the adoption driver (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Oz Cloud Agents & Orchestration (Warp docs)](sources/warp-oz-cloud-agents.md): runs incur platform plus compute plus inference charges; personal BYOK not supported for cloud runs; team-managed inference on Business/Enterprise (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Ramp Inspect Architecture 2026: How Background Coding Agents Scale Safely](sources/wavect-ramp-inspect-architecture.md): measure accepted changes per unit of review effort and incident risk, not PRs per day; review capacity and CI become the bottleneck (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Hosting the Agent SDK](sources/anthropic-agent-sdk-hosting.md): first-party: token cost dominates container cost by an order of magnitude; per-session cost tracking available (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness design for long-running application development](sources/anthropic-harness-design-long-running-apps.md): first-party: 20x cost for the full harness on one task (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Context Engineering for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Manus](sources/manus-context-engineering-lessons.md): first-party: KV-cache hit rate is the key production metric (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Pi coding agent locked out](sources/yage-pi-coding-agent-locked-out.md): anecdote: Claude subscription credit works only in Claude Code, so other harnesses pay API rates (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Omnigent contextual policies](sources/databricks-omnigent-contextual-policies.md): soft/hard session cost caps that force a cheaper model; per-user daily caps (vendor claim) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare OS announcement](sources/cloudflare-os-announcement.md): all inference via AI Gateway with attribution and budgets per person/team/workspace (vendor claim) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare AI code review](sources/cloudflare-ai-code-review-opencode.md): $0.20 trivial to $1.68 full review by risk tier; shared context file prevents multiplying tokens (first-party) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Vaughan](sources/danielvaughan-meta-harness-pattern-pi.md): cross-harness delegation can multiply cost ~23-25x internal sessions (independent practitioner) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Warp Oz](sources/warp-oz-multi-harness.md): per-team billing and credit caps, but third-party harness inference bills outside Warp's summaries (vendor docs) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

## docs-as-code-prd: PRDs and specs as files in the repo
Whether product specs live as markdown in git and how consistent that practice is.
- [The AI-native SDLC playbook](sources/claude-ai-native-sdlc-playbook.md): intent and spec live as markdown in an `intent/` folder in the product repo for a single product; a dedicated intent repo only when intent spans many repos (§Stage 1, Infrastructure). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Datadog built a "universal machine tool" for Claude Code](sources/claude-datadog-universal-machine-tool.md): the transition table is "data, not spaghetti control flow"; agents change it and hot-reload it under policy without CI (§Why not just build a CRUD app?). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Spec Kit and spec-driven.md (GitHub)](sources/github-spec-kit-sdd.md): spec is declared the source of truth ('Specifications don't serve code' is the doc's own framing); lives in git, one branch per feature. (user-story-mapping)
- [Specs (Kiro docs)](sources/kiro-specs-docs.md): specs are plain markdown files the agent keeps updated (task status); storage path not stated on the page fetched. (user-story-mapping)
- [Understanding Spec-Driven-Development: Kiro, spec-kit, and Tessl](sources/fowler-bockeler-sdd-kiro-speckit-tessl.md): three levels (spec-first, spec-anchored, spec-as-source); all tools are spec-first, few commit to spec-anchored; spec-kit creates a branch per spec so specs behave like change requests. (user-story-mapping)
- [MADR: Markdown Architectural Decision Records](sources/adr-madr-template.md): sections Context and Problem Statement, Decision Drivers, Considered Options, Decision Outcome (Consequences, Confirmation), Pros/Cons; versioned with code. (user-story-mapping)
- [Cursor is a much better product manager (Lenny's Newsletter)](sources/lenny-cursor-better-product-manager.md): blurb lists 'Why source-controlled markdown files might replace traditional SaaS tools' and a chapter on creating PRDs in Cursor with source control (anecdote; no detail). (user-story-mapping)

## enterprise-admin-controls: Enterprise admin controls across harnesses
The identity, audit, policy, data-retention and cost controls a harness gives an org admin, and on which surfaces they are enforced. It is the baseline a regulated owner compares any build or layer against.
- [Agent identity: a new access model for autonomous, team-wide AI](sources/claude-agent-identity-access-model.md): workspace baseline profile inherited by channels, channel overrides; repo access, connectors, skills/plugins, standing instructions; RBAC on who can invoke; per-channel disable (sections "Inheriting permissions", "Broad... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [The AI-native SDLC playbook](sources/claude-ai-native-sdlc-playbook.md): a worked managed-settings file for a regulated enterprise (deny reads of secrets, OS sandbox with domain allowlist, managed hooks and MCP servers only, an approved plugin marketplace, a minimum version) (§Stage 5, Worked example). (research-claude-resources-articles)

- [Loop engineering: Getting started with loops](sources/claude-loop-engineering.md): verification encoded as a SKILL.md (example "verify-frontend-change"); /goal uses an evaluator model to send Claude back to work until a deterministic criterion is met or a turn cap is hit (sections "Turn-based", "Goal-based"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [New in Claude Managed Agents: dreaming, outcomes, and multiagent orchestration](sources/claude-managed-agents-dreaming-outcomes.md): outcomes: write a rubric, a separate grader evaluates "in its own context window, so it isn't influenced by the agent's reasoning", and the agent iterates; up to 10 points better task success than a standard prompting loop;... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Multi-agent coordination patterns: Five approaches and when to use them](sources/claude-multi-agent-coordination-patterns.md): a verifier "is only as good as its criteria"; loops need a max-iteration limit with fallback to a human or a caveated best attempt (Pattern 1). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Improving skill-creator: Test, measure, and refine Agent Skills](sources/claude-skill-creator-evals.md): evals define test prompts plus "what good looks like"; benchmark mode tracks pass rate, elapsed time and tokens; run after model updates to catch regressions ("Using evals to test and improve skills"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to build a Self-improving Product](sources/departmentofproduct-self-improving-product.md): Amplitude's judge feeds a classifier that predicts human thumbs-up; the tutorial starts with only small code fixes autonomous and raises the threshold "as you build trust" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to develop a Headless Product Strategy](sources/departmentofproduct-headless-product-strategy.md): Rippling's 50+ golden cases judged on functions, path, execution and final answer before its MCP launch (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to Manage AI Agents Effectively](sources/departmentofproduct-managing-ai-agents.md): DoorDash went from about 1 human review a day to 2,000 LLM-judge-graded sessions daily (claimed +8 quality points, regression testing cut from 6h to 20m); Airbnb calibrates its judges to 80-90% agreement with humans. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to Identify Opportunities for AI Automation](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-automation-opportunities.md): verifiability is the lead criterion for automation, credited to an unnamed OpenAI co-founder (likely Karpathy). (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use /loops, /goals and other Powerful Slash Commands as a Non-Engineer](sources/departmentofproduct-loops-goals-slash-commands.md): a good goal states the end state, how it's verified and what must be kept; the agent marks "cause unclear" rather than inferring (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build an AI Agent](sources/departmentofproduct-how-to-build-an-ai-agent.md): three autonomy levels: supervised predefined tasks, conditional autonomy with escalation, full independence (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to test a new AI Model](sources/departmentofproduct-model-sense-testing.md): a PM-kept "Model Sense Notebook" holding a prompt library, a claims-vs-reality changelog and a domain eval suite rerun at each model release (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

- [AI hallucination (Product Talk glossary)](sources/producttalk-ai-hallucination-glossary.md): eval method for synthesis: verbatim-quote check in code plus LLM-as-judge fact checker [audit 2026-10-24]. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

Clustering and routing customer feedback, calls and tickets is the best-evidenced PM-agent job, but needs checks against invented or merged quotes.
- [Agents you can coach: how Asana builds human-agent teams with Claude](sources/claude-asana-agents-you-can-coach.md): Slack product questions become Asana tasks; agent answers from approved guidance with links, files product gaps to the product intake project, and raises enablement tasks when a question repeats ("Three jobs"). (research-claude-resources-articles)

## harness-over-model: The harness, not the model, limits real-world value
Ramp found models were good enough; the preconfigured environment (integrations, skills, memory, UX) decided whether non-experts got value. Central to what a "product agent and harness" is. Related: [[compounding-context-repo]].
- [We Built Every Employee at Ramp Their Own AI Coworker](sources/x-sebgoddijn-glass-article.md): "The Models are Good Enough, The Harness Isn't"; 99% adoption but most stuck (§intro) (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How to get your company AI pilled](sources/x-geoffintech-ai-pilled-article.md): same finding framed as lesson 6, "the harness wasn't" (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp built an AI agent harness in six weeks](sources/thenewstack-ramp-laminar-agent-harness.md): the harness (sessions, sandboxes, connectors, observability, routing) is what Ramp chose to own; models stay swappable (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform](sources/ramp-builders-building-laminar.md): the harness's 15 responsibilities listed; provider-agnostic; own trace-debug UI (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Building an agentic harness that outlasts the model](sources/shopify-engineering-agentic-harness-outlasts-model.md): better models gave more noise; all 30+ candidates in one audit were downgraded; the harness is the durable asset (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Introducing Roast](sources/shopify-engineering-introducing-roast.md): "Non-determinism is the enemy of reliability"; YAML + markdown steps interleaved with a Claude Code CodingAgent (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Learning on the Shop floor](sources/x-tobi-learning-on-the-shop-floor.md): 36%→77% merge rate "did not retrain a model... did not switch models" (self-reported) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Stripe's AI minions ship 1,300 PRs weekly from a Slack emoji (How I AI)](sources/howiai-stripe-minions-kaliski.md): minions succeed because of years of devex: hosted devboxes, CI, docs, a 'blessed path for 90% of the common activities' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): data-agent quality depends on pre-AI investments: tiered data catalog, blessed analytics layer, a warehouse hardened for agent query load (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Improving Deep Agents with harness engineering](sources/langchain-improving-deep-agents-harness-engineering.md): vendor claim: changing only prompt, tools and middleware moved the same model from 52.8% to 66.5% on Terminal Bench 2.0 (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands](sources/anthropic-engineering-scaling-managed-agents.md): first-party: harness assumptions about model weakness go stale as models improve; harness components must be re-tested per model (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness design for long-running application development](sources/anthropic-harness-design-long-running-apps.md): first-party: planner/generator/evaluator harness cost $200 vs $9 solo on one task (20x) and a harness component was removed when the model improved (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Rebuilding Devin for Claude Sonnet 4.5](sources/cognition-devin-sonnet-45-rebuild.md): first-party: one model change forced harness changes (context anxiety, parallel tools); 2x faster, 12% better after rebuild (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [We removed 80% of our agent's tools](sources/vercel-we-removed-80-percent-of-our-agents-tools.md): first-party: simplifying to one bash tool raised success 80% to 100% on five queries, tokens down 37% (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness Engineering: ... Eleven Systems](sources/arxiv-harness-engineering-eleven-systems.md): independent: loop sophistication does not predict benchmark performance; production harnesses invest in scaffolding for safety, reliability and integration (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [OpenAI Introduces Harness Engineering (InfoQ)](sources/infoq-openai-harness-engineering.md): vendor claim: harness = repo docs, linters, layered architecture and observability; about a million lines with no hand-written code (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Scaling Managed Agents](sources/anthropic-scaling-managed-agents.md): harness assumptions expire as models improve (context resets useful on Sonnet 4.5, dead weight on Opus 4.5) (first-party) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Meta-Harness paper](sources/arxiv-meta-harness-optimization.md): harness code is itself searchable/optimisable (independent paper) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Boris Cherny summary (Traces)](sources/traces-boris-cherny-light-cone-summary.md): second-hand counterpoint: scaffolding is wiped out by the next model, so harness features decay (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [How Claude Code works in large codebases: Best practices and where to start](sources/claude-code-large-codebases.md): "the harness—determines how Claude Code performs more than the model alone" (section "The harness matters as much as the model"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Cresta turned CX expertise into an agent builder on the Claude Agent SDK](sources/claude-cresta-agent-builder-evals.md): SDK chosen as "the same agentic development harness" as Claude Code, used programmatically (§intro quote, Renjie Li). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Office Hours: Building for the model that doesn't exist yet (Ramp, with Boris Cherny)](sources/claude-customers-ramp-office-hours.md): Ramp keeps removing scaffolding "because the model has just outgrown the harness" and builds for the model 3-6 months ahead (Rahul, mid and closing answers). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Building agents: When to fold subagents into your main agent loop](sources/claude-fold-subagents-into-main-loop.md): since Opus 4.5 models manage more in one loop; rigid multi-agent structures blocked migrations to newer models; Claude Code's system prompt for advanced models was cut by over 80% (three reasons section). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Agent harness design: 3 patterns for harnessing Claude's intelligence](sources/claude-harness-design-three-patterns.md): "agent harnesses encode assumptions about what Claude can't do on its own, but those assumptions grow stale"; context resets added for Sonnet 4.5's "context anxiety" became "dead weight" with Opus 4.5 ("The future of agent... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Product management on the AI exponential](sources/claude-pm-on-the-ai-exponential.md): todo-list reminder hack removed when the next model did it unprompted; system prompt and tool descriptions trimmed with each model, including a 20% reduction for Opus 4.6 ("Do the simple thing"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Improving skill-creator: Test, measure, and refine Agent Skills](sources/claude-skill-creator-evals.md): if the base model passes a capability-uplift skill's evals without the skill, the skill may be retired. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Steering Claude Code: when to use CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, and subagents](sources/claude-steering-claude-code.md): "two separate dials" (model and effort) control capability, while the seven methods control behaviour; each trades context cost against authority (intro; "The seven methods"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Context Engineering for AI Agents Explained - a simple overview of the basics](sources/departmentofproduct-context-engineering-basics.md): agent failures "aren't necessarily model failures, but context failures" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Are Agent Harnesses the new "secret sauce" for Product Teams?](sources/departmentofproduct-agent-harnesses-secret-sauce.md): restates Anthropic's solo $9/20 min broken build vs harness $200/6 h working build; "the right harness for last year's model may be over-engineered for this year's" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [What is parallel AI agent coding? An in-depth guide for product teams](sources/departmentofproduct-parallel-agent-coding.md): parallel agents pay off only after investment in CI, docs and staging environments (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to test a new AI Model](sources/departmentofproduct-model-sense-testing.md): defines "scaffolding" (retrieval, human-in-the-loop escalation, domain checks) as what makes a model reliable in production. It credits Box's Levie, second-hand (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

## harness-portability: Harness portability
Whether sessions, skills and context can move between harnesses and between local and cloud without losing history or behaviour.
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): harness outside the sandbox lets Shopify "swap models, runtimes, even languages on the harness side" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Small Models, Massive Wins (Beyond the Pilot)](sources/venturebeat-beyond-the-pilot-farhan-thawar.md): "River ... switches between models"; "I don't care what harness you wanna use" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): a Kai project can be backed by a different API and harness while keeping Kai's features; Kai skills follow the open skill spec (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Stripe Got 83% of Staff Using One AI Agent. Don't Copy Its Sales Numbers.](sources/aifounders-stripe-kai-dont-copy-sales-numbers.md): 'the skills are the durable asset'; keep them exportable from any vendor harness (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Use Claude Code in the cloud (Claude Code on the web docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-cloud-sessions.md): handoff is deliberately asymmetric: cloud to terminal via --teleport (needs clean git state, same repo, same claude.ai account), terminal to cloud only as a new session or via the Desktop app; the terminal copy is a fork that does not sync back (Move tasks between terminal and cloud) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands](sources/anthropic-engineering-scaling-managed-agents.md): credentials are never visible to the harness; git tokens used at sandbox init, MCP OAuth tokens held in a vault behind a proxy (Credential handling) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloud-origin agents have no 'Move to Machine' option (Cursor forum)](sources/cursor-forum-cloud-to-local-handoff.md): staff (2026-06-05) called cloud-to-local for cloud-origin sessions a 'known limitation', 'not being actively built out right now'; workaround is a local agent on the same repo or continuing in the cloud (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Claude Code deletes conversation history after 30 days by default](sources/itdaily-claude-code-30-day-transcript-deletion.md): Anthropic's stated reason is that plain-text transcripts can hold code and credentials, i.e. retention conflicts with auditability (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent Trace (Thoughtworks Technology Radar Vol. 34)](sources/thoughtworks-radar-agent-trace.md): vendor-neutral JSON trace record linking code ranges to contributor type (human/AI/mixed/unknown) and, per the spec's draft, to the originating conversation; works with Git, Mercurial, Jujutsu (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [codex-plugin-cc](sources/openai-codex-plugin-for-claude-code.md): a competing vendor ships a plugin that runs inside Claude Code; shows plugins as a cross-harness delegation channel. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Run Claude Code programmatically](sources/anthropic-claude-code-headless-agent-sdk.md): `--bare` makes headless runs reproducible by skipping hooks, plugins, MCP and CLAUDE.md. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [MCP spec 2026-07-28](sources/mcp-spec-2026-07-28-key-changes.md): stateless transport and extension mechanism; Client ID Metadata Documents replace dynamic client registration. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Anthropic cracks down on unauthorized Claude usage by third-party harnesses](sources/venturebeat-anthropic-third-party-harness-crackdown.md): independent: Jan 2026 block of subscription OAuth outside official clients (OpenCode and others) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent SDK overview](sources/anthropic-agent-sdk-overview.md): first-party: SDK runs the Claude Code binary; Claude models only; third-party products must use API keys, not claude.ai login (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness Engineering: ... Eleven Systems](sources/arxiv-harness-engineering-eleven-systems.md): independent: portability costs a maintained per-provider conditioning layer (cache breakpoints, thinking tiers); SKILL.md in 9 of 11 harnesses (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [AI SDK: Agents overview](sources/vercel-ai-sdk-agents-docs.md): first-party: HarnessAgent runs Claude Code, Codex or Pi behind one interface (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Omnigent launch](sources/databricks-omnigent-meta-harness-launch.md): one-line YAML change ports a custom agent across harnesses; Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenAI/Claude Agents SDK (vendor claim) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Vercel AI SDK Harnesses](sources/vercel-ai-sdk-harnesses.md): HarnessAgent swaps claudeCode/codex/pi in code, sessions resumable; experimental (vendor docs, June 2026) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Zed ACP](sources/zed-agent-client-protocol.md) and [ACP Registry](sources/zed-acp-registry.md): editor-to-agent standard; 50+ agents; Claude Code and Codex via adapters (vendor/community docs, registry 2026-01-28) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
