- [How Warp builds self-improving agents on Claude](sources/claude-warp-self-improving-agents.md): feedback "typically disappears when the session ends"; the improver skill turns accumulated human feedback into skill edits so "the next run of the inner skill inherits the improvement" (section "Agent self-improvement loops... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to Build Powerful Internal AI Productivity Tools](sources/departmentofproduct-internal-ai-tools-ramp-glass.md): worked SaaS example where a senior PM's research-to-prioritised-spec skill is reused by every PM; a city-launch skill sets the baseline for each new market (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

## outcome-measurement-gap: Nobody can yet measure PM-agent outcomes
Time-saved claims are self-reported; no one publishes decision-quality or outcome measures. An opening for a harness that bakes in measurement.
- [Shopify's River shows why agent context costs more (Magica)](sources/magica-shopify-river-agent-context-cost.md): names the missing evidence: resolution time, rollback rate, retention, infrastructure cost against a baseline (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How River takes security work from a fix to merge](sources/shopify-engineering-river-vulnerability-remediation.md): "PR count and green-branch count measure motion, not remediation"; measure items reaching fixed, rejected or escalated (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): Kai's outcome numbers are within-person usage comparisons (Kai weeks vs non-Kai weeks; power vs low users), not controlled tests (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Emily Glassberg Sands on Latent Space](sources/latentspace-emily-sands-stripe.md): Sands (Oct 2025): 'I have a really hard time understanding impact. Like I don't quite know what statistic to look at' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [The 2026 State of AI Agents Report](sources/claude-2026-state-of-ai-agents.md): 80% "agree" their agent investment has "already delivered measurable financial impact", but no method or metric is defined; only 20% cite unclear ROI as a barrier (ch. 3, ch. 4). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How ABC Legal turned every employee into a builder with Claude Managed Agents](sources/claude-abc-legal-managed-agents-builders.md): each agent reports its own value in hours and dollars to a data warehouse on every run, tracked as an efficiency ratio of value to cost; agents follow a J-curve ("Why Claude Managed Agents"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Measure Claude Code's impact with contribution metrics](sources/claude-code-contribution-metrics.md): the metric is activity (PRs, lines), not outcomes; Anthropic concedes PRs are "an incomplete measure of developer velocity" and positions them as a proxy ("How we're shipping at Anthropic"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [A guide to cost visibility and control in Claude](sources/claude-cost-visibility-control.md): cost-per-outcome recommended, but what work would have cost without AI is business-specific and vendor-unmeasurable (opening section). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [A conversation with Seth Hain about Epic's internal AI adoption](sources/claude-customers-epic-internal-adoption.md): monitoring draft acceptance: 100% unedited use and 0% use are both signs something is wrong (answer on clinical trust). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Office Hours: Asynchronous coding and the end of the IDE with Spotify](sources/claude-customers-spotify-office-hours.md): 75%+ improvement in PR frequency and 73% AI-authored PRs claimed; connecting PRs to work items, A/B tests and user value is "what we're trying to build right now" (ROI segment). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Scaling agentic coding across your organization](sources/claude-guide-scaling-agentic-coding.md): ROI chapter offers sprint throughput, time-to-completion, migration speed, satisfaction surveys, onboarding speed and fewer engineering dependencies for prototyping, plus Activity Metrics (lines accepted, accept rate, DAU,... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Deploying AI from pilot to production: a practical blueprint for CIOs and technical leaders](sources/claude-pilot-to-production-cio-blueprint.md): cites Accenture Tokenomics (September 2026): 42% of organisations share IT and finance accountability with no single owner for AI costs and outcomes, making success hard to measure. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Running an AI-native engineering org](sources/claude-running-ai-native-engineering-org.md): suggested metrics are onboarding ramp time, PR cycle time and Claude-assisted commits, with the warning "don't confuse throughput with success" (How to know your new processes are sticking). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Turning conversation into knowledge: how Slack builds human-agent teams](sources/claude-slack-human-agent-teams.md): token usage "tells you the lights are on"; usage is a pulse check, not proof of value; linking use to results takes "a lot of leaps of faith" (section "Measure outcomes, not activity"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to build a Self-improving Product](sources/departmentofproduct-self-improving-product.md): ship rate vs "would do" rate as a measure, plus a per-change outcome log (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to test a new AI Model](sources/departmentofproduct-model-sense-testing.md): Claude read "this year" as 2024 in a Google Analytics task, and only a hand check of the numbers caught it (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [AskNicely cuts analysis time by 75% with Amplitude AI](sources/amplitude-asknicely-story.md): Time saved only (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Tempo customer story (Atlassian)](sources/atlassian-tempo-customer-page.md): Task-completion/time-savings framing, no decision-quality measure (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [From rowing to steering: how Atlassian's PMs are expanding their role (Dealroom summary)](sources/dealroom-atlassian-rowing-to-steering-summary.md): summary repeats that Atlassian has not figured out how to measure AI-driven impact (confirmed by transcript). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [38 Atlassian AI statistics for 2026](sources/deviniti-atlassian-ai-statistics-2026.md): Hours-saved and adoption counts only (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Meta VP's personal agents (Lenny's Newsletter write-up of The Skip Podcast)](sources/lenny-newsletter-meta-chawla-pm-leader-agents.md): no independent metrics; system was inaccurate at first and needed about six months of nightly tuning. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Roles aren't converging—they're expanding | Tamar Yehoshua (Atlassian CPO)](sources/lenny-podcast-tamar-yehoshua-roles-expanding.md): "we haven't figured it out"; measures PRs deployed, features delivered, usage, OKRs (19:35-20:35). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The ROI of Notion Agents (Notion Research with MeasuringU)](sources/notion-roi-of-notion-agents.md): Task success 93% vs 59%, 38% less time; task-level, not PM outcomes (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Introducing Spark: AI product management agent (Productboard)](sources/productboard-introducing-spark.md): No outcome data (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The bottleneck keeps shifting: what AI is changing about how we build (Gamma interview)](sources/atlassian-bottleneck-keeps-shifting-gamma.md): Gamma's A/B tests showed evals missed a customer preference, so human validation stays. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [State of Product 2026 webinar and event pages (Atlassian)](sources/atlassian-state-of-product-2026-webinar-event.md): Time saved is not translating into strategy time or demonstrable outcomes (event page). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [AI in Product Management: What 379 Product Managers Revealed About the New Reality](sources/productboard-ai-in-product-management-report.md): Only 40% measure AI ROI via business outcomes. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Product Focus Industry Survey Report 2026](sources/productfocus-industry-survey-2026.md): 97% report some productivity improvement from AI (32% significant) but only 64% report improved product outcomes (PDF read in audit). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The State of AI for Product Managers 2026](sources/productside-state-of-ai-for-pms-2026.md): Adoption without strategy or demonstrable outcome. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [State of AI in Product Management 2026](sources/uxcam-state-of-ai-in-product-management-2026.md): 70% of leaders grew AI budgets but only 6% set AI OKRs. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The AI Productivity Paradox](sources/svpg-ai-productivity-paradox.md): cites Atlassian State of Teams 2026 (89% of execs say AI sped work, 6% can show org-wide ROI); output up, outcomes flat (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Experimentation, AI and the Product Model](sources/svpg-experimentation-ai-product-model.md): cheaper building means more shipping without matching outcome gains; measure experimentation by impact, not test volume (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Agentic Software Development Takes The Lead (Forrester)](sources/forrester-agentic-software-development-sdlc-agents.md): 30-40% coding gains vs under 10% team productivity when planning/testing/release stay manual; no source or method given (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Productboard Spark support article](sources/productboard-spark-support-article.md): 7/14/30-day post-release impact reviews "rolling out progressively after GA" (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Introducing Productboard Spark, AI Built for Product Teams](sources/productboard-introducing-spark-agentic-product-system.md): "Post-launch evaluation" promised within days of shipping, labelled [Beta] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Customer Stories (ChatPRD)](sources/chatprd-customer-stories.md): Every metric is drafting speed; none on PRD quality or product outcome (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Helping every team succeed in the AI era (Atlassian blog)](sources/atlassian-blog-helping-every-team-succeed-ai-era.md): Time-per-item and hours-per-week only; no quality or outcome measure (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## pm-ai-usage-surveys: What surveys say about PMs' AI use
Self-selected, mostly vendor-run surveys of where PMs use AI and what they save; directional only.
- [The 2026 State of AI Agents Report](sources/claude-2026-state-of-ai-agents.md): 500+ technical leaders (engineering leaders, IT executives), late 2025; respondents are technical, not PMs (Foreword, Survey methodology). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Building AI agents for the enterprise](sources/claude-building-agents-enterprise-cowork.md): cites Anthropic Economic Index (Sept 2025): 40% of US employees report using AI at work, up from 20% in 2023 (opening). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How people are using Claude Cowork](sources/claude-how-people-use-cowork.md): category shares from 1.2M sampled sessions, 600,000+ organisations, May 11-31 2026, 20-category taxonomy ("What the data shows", "How we measured"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [State of Product 2026 webinar and event pages (Atlassian)](sources/atlassian-state-of-product-2026-webinar-event.md): Report: half save 10-60 minutes a day ('up to 2 hours' is the top bucket); reactive, short-term work; many feel burnt out (single wave); 84% concerned their products won't succeed in market. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [AI tools are overdelivering: results from our large-scale AI productivity survey](sources/lennys-newsletter-ai-tools-overdelivering-results.md): Top PM AI uses: writing PRDs 21.5%, mockups/prototypes 19.8%, communication 18.5%; user research 4.7%, roadmap ideas 1.1%. Largest demand gap is user research (+27.2 points); prototyping desired use rises 19.8% to 44.4%. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [AI tools are overdelivering: results from our large-scale AI productivity survey](sources/lennys-newsletter-ai-tools-overdelivering-results.md): 63% of PMs and 83% of founders report saving 4+ hours/week; over 70% of PMs and founders (combined) report quality gains; designers, the most sceptical group, 47.5% save 4+ hours; engineers' top use is writing code (51% current). More than half of all responde (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Inside Atlassian's State of Product 2026: key takeaways](sources/mindtheproduct-atlassian-state-of-product-2026-takeaways.md): 80% of teams do not involve engineers in ideation, problem definition or roadmap creation; 49% lack time for strategic planning and roadmap development (Atlassian vendor survey, 700 manager-level respondents US/DE/FR plus 521-PM AI survey). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [AI in Product Management: What 379 Product Managers Revealed About the New Reality](sources/productboard-ai-in-product-management-report.md): Largest time savings for presentations, PRDs, competitive research and roadmap creation; about 4 hours saved per task on average; 98% have changed or plan to change team structures; top rising skills data literacy 58% and customer-insight synthesis 54%. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Product Focus Industry Survey Report 2026](sources/productfocus-industry-survey-2026.md): 677 respondents, 40 countries. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The State of Product Management Report 2026 (ProductPlan with Product-Led Alliance)](sources/productplan-state-of-product-management-2026.md): 'Over 60% of prioritization frameworks are overridden by leadership escalations' (marketing page; report gated). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The State of AI for Product Managers 2026](sources/productside-state-of-ai-for-pms-2026.md): 4 in 5 PMs use AI regularly but only 1 in 4 have a strategy to show for it. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [State of AI in Product Management 2026](sources/uxcam-state-of-ai-in-product-management-2026.md): 99% use AI and 70% spend 5+ hours a week with it (search/page figures as reported). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Product Manager Practices for Delegating Work to Generative AI](sources/arxiv-pm-delegating-work-to-genai.md): 62% of 885 Microsoft PMs use GenAI daily; self-report matches telemetry only moderately (rho 0.37); top barrier is output quality (47%) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## pm-job-stable-methods-change: The PM job is stable; how it is done is changing
Surveys and practitioners agree the core PM jobs (discovery, shaping, spec, prioritization, comms, metrics) persist; agents change who or what performs the sub-tasks. Frames which jobs to build job/persona agents for.
- [Product management on the AI exponential](sources/claude-pm-on-the-ai-exponential.md): the traditional playbook assumes what's possible at project start holds at the end; exponential model gains break that, so the PM's job becomes creating clarity in ambiguity and identifying "the handful of true... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to become "AI fluent"](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-fluency.md): Zapier's rubric marks manual-only work and dismissing AI as "unacceptable" for every role, product included (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Cowork plugins (including Product Management plugin)](sources/anthropic-cowork-plugins-product-management.md): PM plugin packages spec writing, roadmap prioritization and progress tracking as skills; research preview, no outcomes stated. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Product development in the agentic era](sources/anthropic-product-development-agentic-era.md): PM job shifted from alignment work (meetings, status reports, ticket backlogs) toward product craft. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How Block is becoming the most AI-native enterprise (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-block-dhanji-goose.md): org-structure change boosted productivity more than AI tools (speaker claim). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Roles aren't converging—they're expanding | Tamar Yehoshua (Atlassian CPO)](sources/lenny-podcast-tamar-yehoshua-roles-expanding.md): "the job of a PM is really the same as it always was... It's how we do it that's changed" (02:30). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Marty Cagan interview (Modern CTO)](sources/moderncto-marty-cagan-2026.md): bottleneck moved from building to deciding. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Ten things I brought back from the Lenny & Friends Summit 2026](sources/productmanagementsociety-ten-things-lenny-summit.md): 'rowing vs steering' framing of PM role. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [An Introduction to Outcome-Driven Innovation](sources/customerthink-outcome-driven-innovation-intro.md): The job, not the product, is the unit of analysis; a job map captures all customer needs (importance/satisfaction ratings not described on this page). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Summary: Continuous Discovery Habits (Evan Samek Substack)](sources/evansamek-continuous-discovery-habits-summary.md): Continuous discovery minimum: weekly customer touchpoints by the team building the product, running small research activities toward a desired outcome; unit is the product trio. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Clay Christensen's Milkshake Marketing](sources/hbs-christensen-milkshake-marketing.md): Customers 'hire' products for a job; segmenting by product category or demographics misses the purchase trigger. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Intercom on Jobs-to-be-Done (book announcement)](sources/intercom-jobs-to-be-done-book.md): JTBD covers switching behavior, real competitors, product scope, identifying the core job and Job Stories; says it is not a step-by-step guide. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Des Traynor on JTBD Radio](sources/jtbd-radio-des-traynor.md): Traynor: the customer isn't the fundamental unit of analysis; 'a job is more like a verb' is Bob Moesta's line, which Traynor endorses. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Getting to a team-based approach to continuous discovery (Teresa Torres)](sources/mindtheproduct-torres-team-based-continuous-discovery.md): Continuous discovery: weekly customer touchpoints by the team building the product, small research activities, in pursuit of a desired outcome; product trio as unit. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How to Build High-Functioning Teams (Pragmatic Institute)](sources/pragmatic-institute-high-functioning-teams.md): 37 product management and product marketing activities, each completed and handed off; Pragmatic's framework page arranges them as 37 boxes in 7 categories, including Market Problems and Win/Loss Analysis. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [More valuable, less protected](sources/reforge-more-valuable-less-protected.md): Spec now more important because building is cheap; speed amplifies the cost of a wrong direction. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The AI Productivity Paradox](sources/svpg-ai-productivity-paradox.md): the fix is the existing product model applied with AI, not a new role (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How AI will impact product management](sources/lenny-how-ai-will-impact-product-management.md): the PM as orchestrator; keep soft skills, use AI to amplify hard skills (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## pm-persona-role-expansion: PM and adjacent personas are expanding or blurring
Evidence on how PM, designer, engineer, founder-PM and PMM roles overlap or expand with AI; bears on persona-based agents.
- [Gumroad's customer support team ships code with Claude](sources/claude-customers-gumroad-support-ships-code.md): the founder predicts artists, writers and engineers will be "promoted to directors, editors, and product managers" (Looking forward). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Inside Rakuten's plan to turn every employee into a builder with Claude Managed Agents](sources/claude-customers-rakuten-every-employee-builder.md): PM Shoko Sakamoto builds multi-cloud FinOps pipelines and stakeholder dashboards and sets up ambient observability agents "all by herself" (Galileo answer). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How a non-technical project manager built and shipped a stress management app with Claude Code in six weeks](sources/claude-nontechnical-pm-ships-app.md): he now commits code releases and ships features at Mythical Games, and a small internal team there delivers work "entirely through Claude" ("Founder mode at work"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Product management on the AI exponential](sources/claude-pm-on-the-ai-exponential.md): roles blend: designers ship code, engineers make product decisions, PMs build prototypes and evals. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Running an AI-native engineering org](sources/claude-running-ai-native-engineering-org.md): "Our PMs code a lot now"; engineers take on content and design; hiring indexes on creative builders with product sense and deep systems experts, less on raw throughput (Team makeup). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to Build Powerful Internal AI Productivity Tools](sources/departmentofproduct-internal-ai-tools-ramp-glass.md): an emerging "internal AI specialist" role at OpenAI, Figma, Replit and Ramp (second-hand) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to "vibe code"](sources/departmentofproduct-vibe-coding.md): three team scenarios; the author leans to designer-led, with PMs overseeing several squads "including eventually, autonomous AI teams" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [What is parallel AI agent coding? An in-depth guide for product teams](sources/departmentofproduct-parallel-agent-coding.md): claim that PMs, as "mini orchestrators", could judge parallel agents' output and run feature variants as experiments (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Claude Design is here](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-design.md): reads model-native design tools as "closing the gaps between each of the traditional product disciplines" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Marty Cagan on AI in product management (airfocus)](sources/airfocus-cagan-ai-product-management.md): Cagan: the delivery-process product-owner role is easy for an AI assistant to dent; product leaders 'need to drive this whole discussion' (P2). 'Theater' is not on this page (see svpg-product-management-theater). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How AI turns product managers back into builders](sources/atlassian-ai-turns-pms-into-builders.md): Prototyping as a PM job in the founder-PM persona (P3). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The bottleneck keeps shifting: what AI is changing about how we build (Gamma interview)](sources/atlassian-bottleneck-keeps-shifting-gamma.md): Gamma co-founder Jon Noronha: ~1 PM to 4 engineers (article sets it against a 1:10 rule of thumb); half of Gamma's PMs and designers commit code; Noronha calls his job 'context wrangler'. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The Definitive Chief Product Officer Job Description (LaunchNotes)](sources/launchnotes-cpo-job-description.md): CPO collaborates with the C-suite, is measured on KPIs, shapes the roadmap, manages PMs and designers (board communication and product ops not on the page). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [AI tools are overdelivering: results from our large-scale AI productivity survey](sources/lennys-newsletter-ai-tools-overdelivering-results.md): Founders report highest satisfaction, with productivity and decision support as top use (32.9%); designers use AI most for research synthesis (22.3%) and content (17.4%). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [What does product operations do? (Parallel HQ)](sources/parallelhq-what-does-product-operations-do.md): Product ops covers processes, tools and data: standardises workflows and documentation, manages tool standardisation, keeps a single source of truth for the roadmap, maintains metrics/feedback/usage data. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Product launch checklist for product marketers (Product School)](sources/productschool-launch-checklist-product-marketers.md): Checklist addressed to PMMs; launch timing named as a PMM decision; positioning, messaging, tiering and pricing listed without named owners; no source settles who breaks ties. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [More valuable, less protected](sources/reforge-more-valuable-less-protected.md): Prototyping, once dependent on engineering, is now open to PMs and designers; PMs now distribute context so teams decide without roadmap gatekeeping. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The Era of the Product Creator](sources/svpg-era-of-the-product-creator.md): Product creators are those actively shaping the product and tackling product risks, whatever their title; non-creator PMs will be left behind; succeeding alone will be the rare exception. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The Four Big Risks](sources/svpg-four-big-risks.md): Persona accountabilities for IC PM (P1), designer (P6a) and engineering lead (P6b) are drawn from this page. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Platform vs Core vs Technical PM (The Technical PM)](sources/thetechnicalpm-platform-vs-core-vs-technical-pm.md): Platform PM defines and prioritises internal tools, systems and APIs; metrics are developer adoption, reliability and cost; Technical PM writes detailed technical requirements for engineering. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Product Manager Practices for Delegating Work to Generative AI](sources/arxiv-pm-delegating-work-to-genai.md): PMs report prototyping, writing SQL and building agents; PMs move "down the stack" as engineers move up (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Prototypes vs Products](sources/svpg-prototypes-vs-products.md): readers report moving from advising on product shape to shaping it directly (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Product Management Theater](sources/svpg-product-management-theater.md): a person "essentially a project manager" declaring they are a product manager "is just pretending" (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## pm-tool-connectivity: Reaching PM tools from agents
MCP/auth/permission reality of getting agents into analytics, research and docs tools, plus tool-sprawl evidence.
- [Making Claude Cowork ready for enterprise](sources/claude-cowork-for-enterprise.md): Zapier connected Cowork to its org database, Slack and Jira to surface engineering bottlenecks; Product and Design Ops copied the result; Zoom MCP connector launched. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [HubSpot product and marketing leaders on scaling Claude Cowork](sources/claude-customers-hubspot-cowork.md): "Wire up connectors before you spend time prompting"; PM in Central AI used Cowork to sit over ServiceNow, Asana, Slack, Sheets and security review for connector requests. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Centrally manage authorization for MCP connectors](sources/claude-enterprise-managed-mcp-auth.md): launch connectors include Asana, Atlassian (Jira, Confluence, Teamwork Graph via Rovo MCP), Canva, Figma, Granola, Linear, Supabase; GA update adds Datadog, Notion, Slack, with Exa, Miro, Zoom coming (update note, Built with... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude Marketplace: plugins and connectors, products and agents, and service partners](sources/claude-marketplace.md): Atlassian's Teamwork Graph connector brings Confluence and Jira context; Notion and Salesforce/Slack connectors named (partner quotes). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Building agents that reach production systems with MCP](sources/claude-mcp-production-patterns.md): three connection paths (direct API, CLI, MCP) and why cloud agents reaching auth'd systems land on MCP (section "Connecting agents to external systems"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Skills explained: How Skills compares to prompts, Projects, MCP, and subagents](sources/claude-skills-explained.md): "MCP connects Claude to data; Skills teach Claude what to do with that data" ("What is MCP?"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [What is a Command Line Interface and why do they suddenly matter to product teams?](sources/departmentofproduct-cli-for-product-teams.md): Google Workspace CLI (`gws <service> <resource> <method>`) gives Claude Code all of Workspace plus workflow commands; auth setup is "fiddly" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build the ultimate Product Dashboard that generates stakeholder updates on demand](sources/departmentofproduct-product-dashboard-stakeholder-updates.md): Slack and Gmail wiring is left as a prompt asking the agent what credentials it needs (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Are Agent Harnesses the new "secret sauce" for Product Teams?](sources/departmentofproduct-agent-harnesses-secret-sauce.md): progressive tool disclosure (Square); Stripe Toolshed's ~500 tools with a curated subset for each agent (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to develop a Headless Product Strategy](sources/departmentofproduct-headless-product-strategy.md): Linear's CEO says agent-created MCP issues now outnumber human ones; PostHog reports 50x more headless MCP requests in 6 months (vendor statements) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Practical ways to use MCP at work](sources/departmentofproduct-mcp-at-work.md): Zapier MCP as an aggregator behind one connector, with native connectors as fallback, for a daily briefing (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Perplexity's new Computer...](sources/departmentofproduct-perplexity-computer.md): read/write connectors (Linear, Slack, Notion, Salesforce, Snowflake), which can be embedded two-way in apps the agent builds (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Practical ways to use Claude Routines at work - a Guide for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-routines-for-product-teams.md): connectors listed per routine (Jira/Linear, Slack, Notion, Drive, Intercom/Zendesk via MCP, optionally Salesforce for ARR weighting) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Google's new Ideate Agent for Product Discovery and Ideation](sources/departmentofproduct-google-stitch-ideate-agent.md): Stitch MCP added to Claude Code so the agent can generate and fetch design screens (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Claude Cowork as a Competitive Intelligence System](sources/departmentofproduct-cowork-competitive-intelligence.md): at Feb 2026 the Google Drive connector read only Google Docs under 10MB, main text only (no images, comments or suggestions) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to develop an MCP Product Strategy](sources/departmentofproduct-mcp-product-strategy.md): in mid-2025 Linear's MCP had 5 tools and Notion's 13. Notion reportedly built "AI-first tools" with its own agent team instead of wrapping its v1 API (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Resources (MCP specification 2025-06-18)](sources/mcp-spec-resources.md): spec says resources are application-driven (host decides how to include context) and access controls SHOULD be implemented; Snowflake's managed server supports tools only (see snowflake note), showing resources are not universally (user-story-mapping)
- [Amplitude MCP in Claude Code (Amplitude docs)](sources/amplitude-mcp-claude-code-docs.md): `claude mcp add -t http -s user Amplitude https://mcp.amplitude.com/mcp`, then OAuth via /mcp; EU customers use a different URL and must re-run and re-authenticate to switch. (user-story-mapping)
- [Dovetail MCP (Dovetail developer docs)](sources/dovetail-mcp-server-docs.md): hosted endpoint https://dovetail.com/api/mcp; OAuth 2.1 with protected-resource metadata, or Bearer API token; DCR and CIMD unsupported so some clients must use tokens. (user-story-mapping)
- [Dovetail MCP (Dovetail developer docs)](sources/dovetail-mcp-server-docs.md): read covers search, projects, folders, data entries, docs as markdown, highlights, comments, themes, tags, file URLs; write covers create projects/docs/highlights/comments/tags; docs list no update or delete tools and no rate limi (user-story-mapping)
- [Snowflake-managed MCP server (Snowflake docs)](sources/snowflake-managed-mcp-server-docs.md): server is a database object created by an admin via `CREATE MCP SERVER ... FROM SPECIFICATION`; OAuth security integration must be created manually (no dynamic client registration). (user-story-mapping)
- [Notion MCP (Notion developer docs)](sources/notion-mcp-developer-docs.md): remote MCP hosted by Notion; connection by OAuth; search, read, create, update pages and databases; Claude Code, Cursor and Codex named as clients. (user-story-mapping)
- [Use Looker with MCP, Gemini CLI and other Agents (Google Cloud docs)](sources/google-looker-mcp-toolbox-docs.md): setup needs Looker URL, client ID and secret env vars, or an OAuth application; Google also mentions a Looker-managed MCP server for managed setups (details not read). (user-story-mapping)
- [Trends Shaping Product Management in 2025 (ProductPlan)](sources/productplan-trends-product-management-2025.md): more respondents than 2024 prefer to consolidate; top reasons standardising tools across teams, budget, data silos/poor visibility; strategy, roadmapping, prioritisation most often wanted in one tool. (user-story-mapping)
- [Call the Teamwork Graph API](sources/atlassian-teamwork-graph-call-the-api.md): the graph is 'available through Forge's Preview release phase', callable only from a Forge app (api.asUser().requestTeamworkGraph), with 1-month breaking-change notice; not a direct OAuth endpoint for an external harness. (user-story-mapping)
- [Limitations and considerations (Teamwork Graph)](sources/atlassian-teamwork-graph-limitations.md): Forge apps only, installed in Jira or Confluence, org-admin install; Atlassian intends controls so graph data 'is not egressed from the Atlassian platform'. (user-story-mapping)
- [Atlassian Rovo MCP server: supported tools](sources/atlassian-rovo-mcp-server-supported-tools.md): v2 exposes a few Primary tools plus discover/executeRead/executeWrite/executeDestructive; delete_jira and manage_jira 'disabled by default. An admin must enable'; Confluence has archive but no delete tool. (user-story-mapping)

## policy-enforcement-fail-open: Agent policy layers that fail open
Policy layers enforce only at the seams they hook, and gaps (errors, unparsed actions, internal tools, sub-agents) have defaulted to allow. In a regulated setting, whether a control fails open or closed matters as much as what it expresses. Our coined label.
- [Running auto mode in production](sources/claude-auto-mode-in-production.md): the classifier "does not eliminate risk"; in a red-team set the miss rate fell from 12% to 7%, and broad allow-rules such as `python:*` are set aside in auto mode because they would bypass the classifier (companion:... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Customize Claude Code with mods in TypeScript](sources/claude-code-mods.md): sec-default stops user mods overriding permission deny rules, but admins who load their own mods first must add sec-default back or lose its restrictions (enterprise section). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Inference hooks: inline data loss prevention for Claude Enterprise](sources/claude-enterprise-inference-hooks.md): "Customize failure-policy tolerance, timeouts" lets each org choose what happens when the DLP server is slow or down; the post does not state the default ("Ways to use inference hooks"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Steering Claude Code: when to use CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, and subagents](sources/claude-steering-claude-code.md): prompted "never do this" rules fail under pressure, in long sessions, ambiguity or prompt injection; real guardrails are hooks (PreToolUse exit code 2) and permissions, with managed settings for org-wide enforcement ("When to... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Zero Trust for AI agents](sources/claude-zero-trust-for-ai-agents.md): Ch 02 "impossible, not tedious" test: friction controls (rate limits, extra hops, SMS MFA) fail against patient agentic attackers; Ch 05 cites fail-closed matching for unrecognised commands. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [omnigent-ai/omnigent issues and discussions on shared-session identity, audit evidence and enterprise authorisation (#2150, #5670, #10359, #11493, discussions #5931 and #1133)](sources/github-omnigent-identity-audit-issues.md): The nearest thing to adopter testimony: outside teams evaluating Omnigent for multi-user pilots describe exactly the gaps a regulated audit setting would hit. (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [omnigent-ai/omnigent security advisories and policy-bypass issues](sources/github-omnigent-security-advisories.md): The strongest evidence found on how Omnigent's governance layer behaves under attack. (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [CVE-2026-62676: omnigent Shell-Command Parser Fails Open, Allowing Policy Bypass](sources/securelayer7-cve-2026-62676-omnigent.md): An independent security firm's write-up of Omnigent's first published guardrail CVE. (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)

## prd-agents: PRD and spec writing/review as an agent job
Agents draft and review PRDs and specs; adoption is high but quality evidence is thin and output can be generic.
- [How CodeRabbit used Claude to build an agent orchestration system](sources/claude-coderabbit-plan-orchestration.md): output is a "collaborative product requirements document" validated by stakeholders before implementation (orchestration section). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [HubSpot product and marketing leaders on scaling Claude Cowork](sources/claude-customers-hubspot-cowork.md): Business Systems manager: custom document-formatting skills mean the Business Requirements Document "shows up to the kickoff meeting before we do", then evolves as transcripts are added to the session. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Deploying Claude across your organization: How Anthropic uses Cowork](sources/claude-guide-deploying-cowork-across-org.md): the Product starting point is "PRD drafting from customer feedback and analytics", measured by time to first reviewable draft (ch. 4 table); PRDs drafted from usage data and customer quotes (ch. 6). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to use Claude Code for non-engineering use cases](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-code-non-engineers.md): PRD and Jira-ticket subagents from community templates; a one-line change produced an oversized story (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Google's new Ideate Agent for Product Discovery and Ideation](sources/departmentofproduct-google-stitch-ideate-agent.md): a chosen research finding becomes a short PRD, which becomes the prompt for screen generation (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [ChatPRD guide (Aakash Gupta, with ChatPRD founders)](sources/aakashg-chatprd-guide.md): Drafting from about 2 hours to about 30 minutes (author's own testing, no method) (case 9) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [ChatPRD AI review (Banani)](sources/banani-chatprd-ai-review.md): ChatPRD = AI copilot for writing and reviewing PRDs; ChatGPT with example PRDs is a workable but less convenient alternative (Banani, adjacent-tool vendor) (case 9) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [38 Atlassian AI statistics for 2026](sources/deviniti-atlassian-ai-statistics-2026.md): [audit 2026-10-24: misattributed] The Procore roadmap-item figure (about 1 hour to about 15 minutes) is NOT in this article; it comes from Atlassian's own blog (see atlassian-blog-helping-every-team-succeed-ai-era) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Enterpret launches the first agentic customer feedback platform (Business Wire)](sources/enterpret-agentic-feedback-platform-launch.md): Draft-PRD-from-evidence use case on Enterpret's use-case page (not in the release); anonymised, unsourced examples [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [I tested 5 AI tools to write a PRD](sources/fireside-pm-tested-5-ai-tools-prd.md): Tested ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, ChatPRD on one PRD task (AI tutor); ranking Claude, ChatPRD, Gemini, ChatGPT, Grok (cases 9, 19) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Claude Cowork (InfoQ)](sources/infoq-claude-cowork-plugins.md): Plugin covers specs, roadmaps, stakeholder updates, research synthesis, metrics review, competitive briefs, brainstorming; per repo README, not InfoQ (case 19) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Cursor is a much better product manager (Lenny's Newsletter)](sources/lenny-cursor-better-product-manager.md): PRDs drafted against the real codebase, pushed to Confluence/Notion via MCP, Jira tickets generated (case 20) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Introducing Spark: AI product management agent (Productboard)](sources/productboard-introducing-spark.md): Spark writes specs and pushes them to coding agents via MCP (per product page, not the blog) (case 2) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Product Manager Practices for Delegating Work to Generative AI](sources/arxiv-pm-delegating-work-to-genai.md): drafting documents is the top use (73%), yet specs are treated as high-accountability work and not handed off (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The AI Productivity Paradox](sources/svpg-ai-productivity-paradox.md): using AI to produce PRDs, roadmaps and business cases faster is the weak-team pattern (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

- [Productboard Spark support article](sources/productboard-spark-support-article.md): Drafts specs grounded in strategy and connected codebase (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket/Azure DevOps) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Introducing Productboard Spark, AI Built for Product Teams](sources/productboard-introducing-spark-agentic-product-system.md): "Direct push to your dev tools" (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) labelled [Beta] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Customer Stories (ChatPRD)](sources/chatprd-customer-stories.md): LaunchDarkly ~50% less PRD time, Autodesk initial drafts hours to minutes, CallRail ~90% faster docs; all drafting time, vendor-published (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Claire full time on ChatPRD](sources/chatprd-claire-full-time-on-chatprd.md): Customers described only as "biggest enterprises, startups, and solo devs/PMs", none named (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [6 Free AI PRD Generators Tested 2026](sources/ideaplan-best-free-ai-prd-generators-2026.md): Claims Claude matched ChatPRD (both B+), ChatGPT C, per Aakash Gupta; no link or rubric (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Helping every team succeed in the AI era (Atlassian blog)](sources/atlassian-blog-helping-every-team-succeed-ai-era.md): Procore Staff TPM: quarterly roadmap items "about an hour" each before, "about 15 minutes" with Rovo (vendor-published testimonial) (case 1) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Spec Kit and spec-driven.md (GitHub)](sources/github-spec-kit-sdd.md): templates force `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION: ...]` markers instead of guessing, a spec-quality convention. (user-story-mapping)
- [Understanding Spec-Driven-Development: Kiro, spec-kit, and Tessl](sources/fowler-bockeler-sdd-kiro-speckit-tessl.md): unclear target user (developers, product people, or both); Kiro turned a small bug into 4 stories / 16 acceptance criteria. (user-story-mapping)

## product-artifact-primitives: Native PM artifact objects and project containers across platforms
What each platform treats as its first-class product-work objects (idea, initiative, project, space, spec, insight, document, skill) and how a 'project' is bounded. Matters for deciding whether a product meta-harness defines its own primitives or maps onto existing ones.
- [Projects redesigned: from folder to conversation](sources/claude-code-projects-redesigned.md): project library collects files you add and artifacts Claude produces. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude Cowork and chat are now one Claude](sources/claude-cowork-chat-unified.md): Claude Docs and Claude Slides launched (beta, paid plans), Claude Design available inside conversations; artifacts live at one shareable link, editable directly or by commenting to Claude, exportable to PowerPoint or PDF... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How the product designer who built Claude Design uses it](sources/claude-design-designer-workflow.md): HTML as the universal medium for decks, one-pagers, emails, animations, and "designs that are also their own editors" ("Make it alive"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to use Claude Projects and Skills to Monitor your Product's Health](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-projects-product-health.md): a Project (instructions, knowledge files, history) is the PM's standing container; filename prefixes stand in for structure (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Teamwork Graph glossary (Atlassian developer docs)](sources/atlassian-teamwork-graph-glossary.md): Object = single item of data (Jira work item, Confluence page, Google Drive file); each belongs to an object type that defines structure, properties and possible relationships. (user-story-mapping)
- [Teamwork Graph object types (Atlassian developer docs)](sources/atlassian-teamwork-graph-object-types.md): Queryable API object types named on the page: Jira work items and Users. (user-story-mapping)
- [Getting started with the Atlassian Rovo MCP server](sources/atlassian-rovo-mcp-server-getting-started.md): Server URL https://mcp.atlassian.com/v2/mcp; v1 usage moves to v2 tools on 2027-03-01 (per the page). (user-story-mapping)
- [Atlassian Rovo MCP server: supported tools](sources/atlassian-rovo-mcp-server-supported-tools.md): Jira read: work items, projects, boards, sprints, filters, dashboards, comments, changelogs, worklogs, statuses, versions, components. Write: create/edit/transition work items, comments, links, versio (user-story-mapping)
- [What is a Jira space (formerly project)](sources/atlassian-jira-space-definition.md): 'A Jira space is a collection of related work items' for a product, team, service or project; items carry a space key prefix (e.g. GDT-1). (user-story-mapping)
- [What is a Confluence space](sources/atlassian-confluence-space-definition.md): A space is a container for creating, storing and collaborating on work tied to a team, shared project or initiative; examples: a knowledge base, or a space per launch or campaign. (user-story-mapping)
- [What is an idea (Jira Product Discovery docs)](sources/atlassian-jira-product-discovery-ideas.md): Idea = basic unit of work in a JPD space; fields such as goals, team, priority score, impact. (user-story-mapping)
- [Working with databases (Notion API docs)](sources/notion-api-databases-data-sources.md): Database = container holding data sources and views; does not carry the schema in current API versions. (user-story-mapping)
- [Notion MCP supported tools](sources/notion-mcp-supported-tools.md): Search (up to 50 results), connector search across Slack/Drive/GitHub, memory search over saved agent memories. (user-story-mapping)
- [Projects (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-projects.md): Project = 'a grouping of issues that have a clear outcome or planned completion date'. (user-story-mapping)
- [Initiatives (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-initiatives.md): Initiatives are workspace-level containers for projects tied to a shared objective; IDs like I-<n>. (user-story-mapping)
- [Documents (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-documents.md): Documents attach to projects, initiatives, teams, issues or cycles; same editor as issues; realtime collaboration; version history including agent edits; templates at workspace/team level. (user-story-mapping)
- [Linear for Agents (developer docs)](sources/linear-developers-agents.md): Agents can be @mentioned, assigned issues, comment, and collaborate on projects and documents; installed agents are not billable users. (user-story-mapping)
- [Connect a coding agent to Spark via MCP (Productboard support)](sources/productboard-mcp-server-spark.md): Beta, included with Spark-enabled workspaces at no extra cost; admins enable it under Settings > MCP Server and choose roles. (user-story-mapping)
- [Add features to your hierarchy (Productboard support)](sources/productboard-product-hierarchy.md): Hierarchy: Product > Component > Feature > Subfeature. Features can be imported from spreadsheet, Jira or Zapier. (user-story-mapping)
- [Build on Dovetail (docs)](sources/dovetail-build-on-dovetail.md): Three options: MCP server, REST API (default 200 requests/min per workspace), CLI 'dt' for bulk import from Notion, Confluence, Google Drive and files (no sync after import). (user-story-mapping)
- [github/spec-kit (README)](sources/github-spec-kit-readme.md): Workflow: /speckit-constitution (once per project), then per feature /speckit-specify, -plan, -tasks, -implement, -converge. Runs as skills in the agent's chat. (user-story-mapping)
- [Spec-Driven Development (spec-kit spec-driven.md)](sources/github-spec-kit-spec-driven.md): Each feature lives in specs/<NNN-branch-name>/ with spec.md, plan.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md, tasks.md ([P] marks parallel tasks). (user-story-mapping)
- [About Projects (GitHub Docs)](sources/github-docs-about-projects.md): Project = adaptable table, board and roadmap integrating issues and PRs, at user or organisation level; two-way sync with issues. (user-story-mapping)
- [What are projects? (Claude Help Center)](sources/anthropic-claude-projects-support.md): Project = self-contained workspace: knowledge base (documents, text, code), custom instructions, own chat history; memory mentioned only for a beta version. (user-story-mapping)
- [How Claude remembers your project (Claude Code docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-memory-docs.md): Locations: managed policy (e.g. /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md), user, project (./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md), local (CLAUDE.local.md). (user-story-mapping)
- [Organize work with projects (Claude Cowork docs)](sources/anthropic-cowork-projects-docs.md): Project holds: description (Dispatch reads it to choose a project for a task), folders (one or more local), instructions, links, linked Chat projects, memory. (user-story-mapping)
- [Glean Enterprise Graph (product page)](sources/glean-enterprise-graph-product-page.md): Enterprise Graph = relationships among people, projects, teams, products and processes, plus indexed content metadata; personal graphs infer the tasks and projects behind a person's activity. (user-story-mapping)
- [Scopes (Teamwork Graph API)](sources/atlassian-teamwork-graph-scopes.md): the full API object-type list (one read scope each) covers Jira, Confluence (page, blogpost, comment, database, folder, space, whiteboard), Atlassian Home (goal, goal update, project, project update, tag, comment), Loom, Compass, Focus, Talent and 29 External* connector types; still no idea, PRD, spec, insight or decision type. (user-story-mapping)
- [Relationships (Teamwork Graph)](sources/atlassian-teamwork-graph-relationships.md): four relationship kinds (canonical, activity, logical, inferred); logical ones like AtlassianUserCreatedDocuments unify Confluence pages and external documents under one edge. (user-story-mapping)
- [PRD template (Confluence)](sources/atlassian-confluence-prd-template.md): Atlassian's PRD is a page template whose Options table holds user story, importance and 'Jira issues' as embedded links via /jira; no typed PRD-to-work-item relationship, no JPD or Home link. (user-story-mapping)
- [Atlassian MCP enhancements blog](sources/atlassian-blog-mcp-enhancements-jpd.md): July 2026 blog claims agents can find a JPD idea and link it to a delivery issue, but the supported-tools page names no JPD tool. (user-story-mapping)
- [Open-Inspect README](sources/github-open-inspect-background-agents.md): the session is 'the core unit of work'; it stores messages, events, 'Artifacts | PRs created, screenshots captured', participants and sandbox state; no project object, grouping is by repository, environment and team; Linear holds the project mapping. (user-story-mapping)
- [Why We Built Our Own Background Agent (Ramp Builders)](sources/ramp-builders-why-we-built-our-own-background-agent.md): Inspect's unit is the session (own SQLite DB, shareable by URL) and its output is the PR with before/after screenshots; no spec, PRD, project or folder concept described. (user-story-mapping)

## product-coherence-over-automation: Product coherence can suffer from over-automation
Warnings that agent-driven shipping produces incoherent 'additive' products without a human holding the whole.
- [Office Hours: Building the case for leaders who ship with DoorDash](sources/claude-customers-doordash-office-hours.md): user-facing features need cross-functional buy-in; product/ship/design review now friction; Andy asks "do we even need to have product review?" (learnings answer). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to build a Self-improving Product](sources/departmentofproduct-self-improving-product.md): metric-chasing agents risk wins that harm the experience (Netflix autoplay), "AI optimized product slop" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [DESIGN.md Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-design-md-explained.md): "consistency gets easier but coherence gets harder"; finished-looking AI output suppresses critique. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How do AI coding agents work?](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-coding-agents-explained.md): once engineering capacity stops being the constraint, the risk is "feature slop" and feature discovery becomes the bottleneck. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Someone Behind the Software (Karri Saarinen, Linear)](sources/linear-saarinen-someone-behind-the-software.md): changes are mostly additive and agent-made changes average the product (essay, read); losing learning from struggle is from his summit talk (PMS write-up, secondhand) [audit 2026-10-24]. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Marty Cagan interview (Modern CTO)](sources/moderncto-marty-cagan-2026.md): "product management theater" (title without control over what is built); one-click AI PRDs speed up a bad process; the avoid-thinking remark is from the PMS write-up [audit 2026-10-24]. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Mike Krieger remarks at Lenny and Friends Summit (note.com write-up)](sources/note-krieger-pm-summit-remarks.md): Krieger told a PM "You were 100% right" after the PM covered enterprise customers, customer success and safety; Dill: LLMs give the most likely answer. (Single decision owner and editing-as-a-job are in the PMS write-up, not here) [audit 2026-10-24]. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Ten things I brought back from the Lenny & Friends Summit 2026](sources/productmanagementsociety-ten-things-lenny-summit.md): Saarinen, Krieger, Dill and Cagan remarks on judgment, single decision owner and avoiding thinking (secondhand). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## project-taxonomy: How 'project' is defined
Initiative/project/epic/space taxonomies across tools and conventions.
- [Projects redesigned: from folder to conversation](sources/claude-code-projects-redesigned.md): a project = goal + repo or context + configured environment, connectors, plugins, instructions and model; work is "longer than one reply and has more than one part" (sections "Threads do the work", "Context builds over time"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to use Claude Projects and Skills to Monitor your Product's Health](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-projects-product-health.md): either one Project, or five function-owned sub-Projects plus a master; the master is fed by pasting each sub-Project's summary by hand (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Initiatives (Linear docs)](sources/linear-initiatives-docs.md): Initiatives are curated groups of projects tied to a company objective; sub-initiatives allowed; projects can be collected by filters; initiative health on track/at risk/off track from updates; documents attach via a Resources pro (user-story-mapping)
- [Create a space (Confluence)](sources/atlassian-confluence-create-a-space.md): a space is 'a container ... for work related to a shared project or initiative' with a purpose of Collaboration, Knowledge base or Custom, one owner and a permissions scheme; it is a third 'project'-like container beside Jira spaces and Atlassian Home projects. (user-story-mapping)

## prototyping-agents-limits: Prototyping agents and their limits
Prompt-to-prototype tools let PMs build quickly but break down as complexity grows and need engineering handoff.
- [Harbor: Stripe's AI-assisted prototyping tool](sources/stripe-harbor-ai-prototyping.md): Harbor prototype animation shipped 'nearly one-for-one'; prototypes became inputs to reviews; next step is live data and prototype-scoped databases (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Protodash (How I AI, Owen Williams)](sources/howiai-stripe-protodash-owen-williams.md): gets '90% of the way most of the time ... it will make slop'; taste and craft stay with designers (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Office Hours: Asynchronous coding and the end of the IDE with Spotify](sources/claude-customers-spotify-office-hours.md): prototypes run in real apps with real users and data within an hour or two, but "not every idea ships in an hour"; many need lots of exploration (deployments segment; closing segment). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How the product designer who built Claude Design uses it](sources/claude-design-designer-workflow.md): not for production software (use Claude Code), no image model so poor for logos; left undirected Claude falls back to recognisable house aesthetics ("What Claude Design is not meant to do", "Tell Claude what it should look like"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [The founder's playbook: Building an AI-native startup](sources/claude-founders-playbook.md): prototype existence is not evidence; zero-cost building drives scope creep and "insecure by inexperience" code (Idea and MVP stage challenges). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to build AI Assistant Prototypes](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-assistant-prototypes.md): five vibe-coded clones built from chatbot ideas, then PRD, then a Lovable prompt, with no eval or user test; the author admits the inputs were illustrative (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to "vibe code"](sources/departmentofproduct-vibe-coding.md): Replit couldn't fix a padding bug even from a screenshot; chat-only Lovable leaves non-coders stuck: "works well - until it doesn't" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Google's new Ideate Agent for Product Discovery and Ideation](sources/departmentofproduct-google-stitch-ideate-agent.md): Stitch output is "by no means production-ready"; for discussion only; beta, free with limits (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build a Persona Feature Tester with Claude Code and ElevenLabs](sources/departmentofproduct-persona-feature-tester.md): Claude Design's first pass looked like a brochure until the author redirected it (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Claude Design is here](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-design.md): onboarding, landing page and 3D component were strong from short prompts. The stakeholder deck was "passable" but full of AI clichés, and PPT export failed (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to do AI-powered product discovery sprints](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-discovery-sprints.md): Alloy builds features on a screenshot of the live product and pulls specs from Jira, Linear or Notion (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Choosing your AI prototyping stack (Anna Arteeva)](sources/annaarteeva-choosing-ai-prototyping-stack.md): Practitioner migration Bolt -> v0 -> Lovable, prefers Lovable (case 17) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Figma Make vs Lovable (Playcode)](sources/playcode-figma-make-vs-lovable.md): Competitor (Playcode) comparison, reportedly without hands-on testing; original page now redirects, unverified (case 16) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [AI prototyping with Lovable (Product Talk)](sources/producttalk-ai-prototyping-lovable.md): Visual/brand inconsistency, breakage with complexity, Supabase login ~0.5s to 25s (TimelyCare), tool claiming unmade fixes, prototype looking too real; about half (5 of 11) moved design work to Figma/Stitch/a design system; Cursor only suggested (case 18) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Figma Make review (Salesdorado)](sources/salesdorado-figma-make-review.md): Edge is reading existing Figma files; prototype-only, figma.site hosting, credit quotas strictly enforced per licence since 18 March 2026; no documented test (case 16) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Lovable raises $330M at $6.6B valuation (tech.eu)](sources/techeu-lovable-330m-raise.md): Unnamed ride-sharing and delivery platform: design concept testing "six weeks to five days" (vendor-supplied speed claim, not a limit) (case 18) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Vercel case studies (Avalara)](sources/vercel-case-studies-avalara.md): Avalara "two patent-pending products created in roughly 60 days" (vendor-claim) (case 17) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Prototypes vs Products](sources/svpg-prototypes-vs-products.md): prototypes show nothing about reliability, scale, security, compliance or full business logic; vendor claims are "buyer beware" (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Agentic Software Development Takes The Lead (Forrester)](sources/forrester-agentic-software-development-sdlc-agents.md): PM prototypes are handed "to the rest of the team to productize" (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## public-by-default-agent-work: Public-by-default agent work and its costs
Agent sessions that are visible to the whole organisation by default (no DMs, no private mode), so others learn by watching and the transcripts can be mined; and the costs of that default: questions not asked, sensitive data in open threads, channel membership as access control, regulated walls. Matters for the trust-privacy-defaults and agent-interface choices.
- [Learning on the Shop floor](sources/x-tobi-learning-on-the-shop-floor.md): River "does not respond to direct messages"; "Asking for help feels different when the whole company can see the question" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): "Every conversation with River becomes a public Slack transcript, open by default to other Shopify employees" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [River's reaction to the Shop floor post](sources/x-tobi-river-reaction-to-shop-floor-post.md): "Some questions that would have been asked in a DM just don't get asked"; also an "honesty pressure" on agent and user (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Small Models, Massive Wins (Beyond the Pilot)](sources/venturebeat-beyond-the-pilot-farhan-thawar.md): River refuses private channels too: "you can't go into a private channel and say, 'Hey, River, help me build'" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Quick](sources/shopify-engineering-quick.md): the same default for artifacts: all sites open to all employees, no owners (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify's River shows why agent context costs more (Magica)](sources/magica-shopify-river-agent-context-cost.md): Slack's CPO: a boundary for "genuinely sensitive work"; "psychological safety should determine where openness stops" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify Just Showed the Agent Stack](sources/adaptordie-shopify-river-agent-stack.md): "A pricing conversation may need a tighter audience" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Hacker News: River submissions and comments](sources/hn-shopify-river-discussion.md): one-line anecdote: the way people speak to agents wouldn't be "kosher in a company slack" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [The Transparency Paradox (Bernstein)](sources/asq-bernstein-transparency-paradox.md): broad visibility can breed hiding; privacy zones raised output 10–15% (independent; factory setting) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Create information barriers in Slack](sources/slack-information-barriers-docs.md): chat-tool walls don't stop interaction in shared channels, so a channel-native agent inherits that gap (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Tenable on Claude Tag](sources/tenable-claude-tag-slack-access-model.md): in channel agents, public-channel join policy effectively governs access to the agent's credentials; new members see scrollback (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Agents you can coach: how Asana builds human-agent teams with Claude](sources/claude-asana-agents-you-can-coach.md): Bose argues one-on-one agent use hides the prompt and back-and-forth from reviewers, so they cannot align on or revise the instructions. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Lessons from Anthropic on building effective human-agent teams](sources/claude-building-effective-human-agent-teams.md): Lesson 1: "if it's not written down and accessible, it doesn't exist" for agents; channels default public within the org; a handful of workspace-level boundaries instead of per-item sharing; private DMs and personal-connector... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Turning conversation into knowledge: how Slack builds human-agent teams](sources/claude-slack-human-agent-teams.md): "Agents can only learn from what they can see"; default channels to public and go private on purpose; "A private channel is a blind spot for every agent that reports on it" (sections "Treat your conversation history", "Default... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude Tag now supports personal connectors in channels](sources/claude-tag-personal-connectors.md): "Anything Claude posts is visible to everyone in the channel"; the requester chooses review mode (see the reply before it posts) or auto mode (posts unless Claude judges content sensitive) (intro, §Using personal connectors). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Self-service data analytics in Slack: how Anthropic deploys Claude Tag for ad-hoc questions](sources/claude-tag-self-service-analytics.md): keep the agent in shared channels and work in threads, not DMs, so threads are a reviewable record (section "Claude Tag threads become the new meeting"). (research-claude-resources-articles)

## remote-agent-invocation: Remote agent invocation
Starting and steering agents that run elsewhere: cloud tasks, scheduled or API/webhook-triggered runs, Slack mentions.
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): one stack, three modes: interactive (River), automation (PR review, woken by external systems), job (CI/batch, log optional) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How River takes security work from a fix to merge](sources/shopify-engineering-river-vulnerability-remediation.md): River opens one Slack thread per finding from a ledger; 4 threads / 35 findings in a minute, each progressing independently (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Small Models, Massive Wins (Beyond the Pilot)](sources/venturebeat-beyond-the-pilot-farhan-thawar.md): River is pull-only: "you can talk to it, but it doesn't talk to you" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Stripe's AI minions ship 1,300 PRs weekly from a Slack emoji (How I AI)](sources/howiai-stripe-minions-kaliski.md): minions start from a Slack emoji reaction (message = prompt, emoji picks the repo), also from Docs and tickets, and from a phone (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Harbor: Stripe's AI-assisted prototyping tool](sources/stripe-harbor-ai-prototyping.md): Harbor's toolset is exposed on Stripe's internal MCP so Kai and devbox coding agents can create, read, update and publish prototypes; its renderer is a separate service (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Automate work with scheduled tasks (Claude Code routines docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-scheduled-tasks.md): an API trigger gives a task a /fire HTTP endpoint with a per-task bearer token that returns a session URL; fire text is wrapped as untrusted data (Add an API trigger) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Codex cloud and the Slack integration (OpenAI docs)](sources/openai-codex-cloud-slack.md): Codex cloud tasks run in published environments, in parallel, 'while your computer is asleep'; internet access and secrets configured per environment (cloud docs, learn.chatgpt.com/docs/cloud.md) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Oz Cloud Agents & Orchestration (Warp docs)](sources/warp-oz-cloud-agents.md): triggers from Slack, Linear, schedules, CLI, API/SDK; self-host via managed Docker worker or unmanaged `oz agent run` in CI/Kubernetes (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol Specification](sources/a2a-project-specification-v1.md): v1.0.0; Agent Card discovery, task lifecycle incl. INPUT_REQUIRED/AUTH_REQUIRED, streaming and push webhooks; identity/credential issuance left to implementers (first-party spec). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [LF A2A one-year release](sources/linuxfoundation-a2a-one-year-press-release.md): 150+ supporting orgs, v1.0, Azure Foundry/Copilot Studio and Bedrock AgentCore integrations; no named end-user production deployment (vendor claim). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [A2A adoption, hype and reality](sources/glukhov-a2a-adoption-hype-reality.md): independent: no named production deployments; 'supported by' is not 'used in production'; proposes four adoption tiers. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Ask HN: Is anyone using A2A?](sources/hn-ask-is-anyone-using-a2a.md): anecdote: some enterprise/Google-ecosystem use, many reports of returning to MCP or plain HTTP; 'no A2A in any final product' at one large company. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Copilot Studio A2A](sources/microsoft-copilot-studio-a2a.md): a shipping enterprise orchestrator consumes external A2A agents with API key/OAuth; customer responsible for permissions and oversight (vendor docs). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [AgentCore Runtime A2A](sources/aws-bedrock-agentcore-runtime-a2a.md): managed hosting of A2A servers with SigV4/JWT auth (vendor docs). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [MCP Tasks extension](sources/mcp-ext-tasks-long-running-operations.md): durable task handle, polling, input_required; the MCP-native answer to host timeouts for agent-like tools (first-party spec). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [MCP spec 2026-07-28 changes](sources/mcp-spec-2026-07-28-key-changes.md): stateless MCP; Sampling deprecated so an MCP-served agent must bring its own model; tasks become an extension (first-party spec). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Glean agents as MCP tools](sources/glean-agents-as-mcp-tools.md): admin-curated agents exposed to Claude Desktop/Cursor/VS Code only if read-only, no human-in-the-loop, finishing in ~30s because hosts time out (vendor docs). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Claude Code MCP docs](sources/anthropic-claude-code-mcp-tasks-oauth.md): calls >2 min auto-background; MCP Tasks (public beta, v2.1.304+) continue on the server; non-interactive runs cancel input requests (vendor docs). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Codex as an MCP server (removed)](sources/openai-codex-mcp-server-removed.md): OpenAI removed `codex mcp-server`; replacement app server is experimental and not MCP, so wrapping a coding harness as an MCP agent is not a stable vendor route (first-party docs). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [codex-plugin-cc](sources/openai-codex-plugin-for-claude-code.md): official OpenAI plugin lets Claude Code delegate reviews/tasks to Codex via the app server, locally; cross-harness delegation without a remote protocol (first-party). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Run Claude Code programmatically](sources/anthropic-claude-code-headless-agent-sdk.md): `claude -p` with JSON/schema output, cost in result, `--bare`; unattended runs deny permission prompts (vendor docs). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Claude Code GitHub Actions](sources/anthropic-claude-code-github-actions.md): event-driven, plugin-skill-as-prompt reviewer on a CI runner; OIDC federation avoids stored keys (vendor docs). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cursor Cloud Agents API](sources/cursor-cloud-agents-api.md): public beta REST API with SSE and steering; webhooks not yet in v1 (vendor docs). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Jules REST API](sources/google-jules-api.md): v1alpha sessions/activities API (vendor docs). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Copilot cloud agent](sources/github-copilot-cloud-agent.md): one repo, one PR, 59-minute cap per session (vendor docs). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Willison async coding agents](sources/simonwillison-async-coding-agents-tag.md): independent usage log and PRarena merge-rate comparison (2025-10-01). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Hosting the Agent SDK](sources/anthropic-agent-sdk-hosting.md): Track 3 view: hosting a deployed Claude-based task agent means one long-lived subprocess per session and token cost >> container cost (vendor docs). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare Agents Week recap](sources/cloudflare-agents-week-in-review.md): Managed OAuth for Access (RFC 9728) lets agents act on a user's behalf without service accounts; Mesh scoped private access (vendor claim, 2026-04-20) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare Sandbox docs](sources/cloudflare-sandbox-sdk-docs.md): coding-agents guide for running Claude Code, Codex or Devin in a per-task sandbox (vendor docs; details not read) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare AI code review](sources/cloudflare-ai-code-review-opencode.md): a task-specific multi-agent reviewer on OpenCode, run as a CI component; 131k runs, $1.19 average (first-party production account) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agentic coding is straining CI. Here's how we scaled test impact analysis at Anthropic](sources/claude-ci-test-impact-analysis.md): the monitoring session was event-triggered (lag threshold) and resumed the conversation, rather than started by a person ("Patch 2"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Projects redesigned: from folder to conversation](sources/claude-code-projects-redesigned.md): threads run in the cloud and are steerable from a phone; local threads "coming very soon". (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude Cowork on web and mobile: hand off work anywhere](sources/claude-cowork-web-mobile-handoff.md): scheduled tasks "now run with no device online", e.g. Monday client prep at 6am leaving a follow-up email drafted but unsent (section "What changes today"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Brainlabs gave 1k+ marketers at its media agency an AI coworker with Claude Cowork and skills](sources/claude-customers-brainlabs-cowork-skills.md): Managed Agents inside Notion fire when board items change state; a Notion agent tags complex tickets "Claude" and a managed "Get Stuff Done" agent picks them up using the skills library and Slack and Calendar connectors... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Delivery Hero's agent merges 100+ pull requests a day with Claude](sources/claude-customers-delivery-hero-pr-agent.md): Herogen "picks up tasks assigned through Jira", writes code, iterates on tests, submits a PR; roadmap adds Slack handoffs and calling it into existing PRs (§The outcome, §Looking ahead). - [Office Hours: Building for the model that doesn't exist yet (Ramp, with Boris Cherny)](sources/claude-customers-ramp-office-hours.md): Inspect is invoked by @-mention in Slack threads, via web, and increasingly by automations; "more Inspect sessions are coming from automations than humans" (Rahul, late in transcript). ## research-synthesis-agents: Research synthesis agents
AI synthesis of interviews, surveys and calls; time saved is claimed, but fidelity and hallucination risk are documented.
- [Sourcegraph streamlines product and community insights with Claude](sources/claude-customers-sourcegraph-product-insights.md): output keeps a high-level view "while still allowing us to link directly to specific feedback sources". (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to build a Persona Feature Tester with Claude Code and ElevenLabs](sources/departmentofproduct-persona-feature-tester.md): a Claude Project loaded with NN/g articles derives five personas from the research folders (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use Google's new Ideate Agent for Product Discovery and Ideation](sources/departmentofproduct-google-stitch-ideate-agent.md): Claude Code reads research transcripts and shortlists three product changes (the transcripts were mock) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to do AI-powered product discovery sprints](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-discovery-sprints.md): AI-moderated interview tools (Strella, Askable, Listen) run sessions at scale and write the synthesis. Amazon reportedly uses Strella (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [LLM vs human extraction error rates (arXiv 2508.09458)](sources/arxiv-llm-qualitative-extraction-error-rates.md): AI inaccuracies 1.51% vs 4.37% for humans when extracting data from published papers for a scoping review (not Dovetail, not interviews) [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

- [Dovetail review 2026 (CleverX)](sources/cleverx-dovetail-review-2026.md): Competitor view (no test): Dovetail AI adds less value on small datasets; no recruitment; per-seat cost [audit 2026-10-24] (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Dovetail announces world-first AI customer insights hub](sources/dovetail-ai-customer-insights-hub.md): AI transcription, summaries, highlight clustering and auto-analysis (case 5) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Dovetail announces world-first AI customer insights hub](sources/dovetail-ai-customer-insights-hub.md): Launch-release testimonials: Notion PM Eric Liu "from 100 hours down to 10"; GrandPad "gone down by about half" per interview (vendor-claim) (case 5) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

- [Maze AI moderator](sources/maze-ai-moderator.md): AI-moderated interviews and AI analysis (case 11) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

- [How AI will impact product management](sources/lenny-how-ai-will-impact-product-management.md): discovery 3/5: AI finds signal in customer data, but customers still want people (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
